a2953.t:
GoL’s Chief Engine House Recounts Achievements -Finance Ministry Reports Positive Fiscal Outlook, Rising Growth
MONROVIA – If there is one public institution that merit the epithet, “Maradona of Liberia’s Public Sector”, or “Midfield Mastro of Government Development” it is the Ministry of Finance. Even though criticisms abound amongst ordinary citizens they are yet to feel the impact of Government and the economy, the Ministry of Planning and Development Planning insists that the macroeconomic indicators are assuring, all pointing upwards. In a synopsis of its 2024 achievements, the Ministry zeroed on how its nailed inflation, triggered growth, ballooned government revenue envelops, and accelerated MCC results, amongst other things. See below for the full text of MFDP Achievements for 2024.
MFDP Achievements for 2024:
At the end of the 2024 which is the fist year of the Boakai Administration, the Ministry of Finance and Development Planning (MFDP) is pleased to avail achievements it made in the period under review including the stabilization of the economy, lowering inflation, crafting of the National Development Plan, payment of civil servants in time for Fiscal Year 2024 and negotiation leading to the announcements of Liberia’s Second Millennium Challenge Cooperation Compact. The fiscal house also recorded in 2024 strong fiscal performance and the initiation of fiscal decentralization.
Economic Overview:
In 2024, the Ministry of Finance and Development Planning (MFDP) focused on advancing Liberia’s economy, achieving a growth rate of 5.1 percent. This growth was supported by strong performances in key sectors such as mining, agriculture, fisheries, and services.
The economy is projected to grow at an accelerated rate of 5.8 percent in 2025. Over the medium term, the average growth rate is expected to be 5.6 percent, driven by robust mining activities, the expansion of services, significant infrastructure investments supported by development partners, and increased economic activity fueled by improved electricity supply.
The government has also begun implementing structural reforms in critical sectors such as energy, trade, transportation, and financial services. These reforms aim to create a more favorable environment for economic activities and investments.
Inflation:
Inflation rate was 10.1% in 2023; current inflation rate is 7.7% on average and projected to further decline to 6.6 percent at the end of the period. While GDP growth rate for 2023 was 4.7%, it grew to 5.1% in 2024 and is expected to rise to 5.8 in 2025. These figures reflect transformational policy interventions being made by the Ministry of Finance & Development Planning to enhance economic growth and development.
Over the past nine months, substantial progress has been made across multiple sectors, particularly in the service industry. This optimistic growth outlook is underpinned by strong performances in various economic sectors. The mining and panning sector is projected to grow by 8.5 percent, manufacturing by 6.9 percent, and agriculture and fisheries by 5.2 percent. The services sector, a critical component of the economy, is expected to grow by 5.0 percent.
Extended Credit Facility (ECF):
During the year, the MFDP led Liberia’s successful accession to the International Monetary Fund’s (IMF) Extended Credit Facility (ECF) program. The IMF Board approved an ECF arrangement for Liberia worth SDR 155 million (approximately US$210 million). This decision includes an immediate disbursement of SDR 4.3 million (about US$5.8 million). The 40-month financing package is designed to support the government’s National Development Agenda (ARREST).
This IMF intervention aims to address macroeconomic imbalances, strengthen debt sustainability, and lay the groundwork for higher, more inclusive and private sector-driven growth, particularly beyond the enclave sector. The ECF arrangement is expected to attract additional external financing from international financial institutions (IFIs) and development partners. Negotiations for the ECF program spanned eight months of the Boakai-Koung Administration, involving staff from the MFDP, the General Auditing Commission (GAC), and the Central Bank of Liberia (CBL).
Payment towards Debt Obligations
Under this new administration, the Ministry of Finance & Development has been responsibly servicing the gargantuan debt obligations it inherited by payments of domestic and external debts, as well as, payments of subscriptions to regional and international bodies to which Liberia has membership.
As of end November 2024, Domestic Debt payment (including obligations to commercial banks) during the course of this Fiscal Year amounts to US$ 36,599,733.00, while External Debt payment amounts to US$47,125,555.00. Additionally, subscriptions payments to regional and international bodies sum up to US$4,312,950.00.
Fiscal Performance:
On the fiscal front, revenue collection has been on target, with the Liberia Revenue Authority (LRA) reporting US$619.9 million by the end of November 2024, achieving 84% of its annual target. Notable revenue achievements included taxes on income and profits (US$137.2 million) and taxes on international trade (US$108.8 million), which were the major contributors to the revenue performance during the year.
Fiscal Decentralization:
The MFDP, in collaboration with the Ministry of Internal Affairs, led initiatives for fiscal decentralization across the country. This included the successful implementation of regulations under the Revenue Sharing Law, which mandates that 40 percent of revenues generated in each county be allocated to County Service Centers.
In addition, the MFDP established an administrative decentralization structure to facilitate the implementation of the Local Government Law. The Local Government Fiscal Board has been set up with the mandate to set annual expenditure ceilings for county administrations. The County Treasuries are progressing as planned, with ten ministries and agencies agreeing to disaggregate their budgets. This will enable the direct transfer of funds to counties, allowing for checks to be received and vouchers processed at the county level.
National Development Plan:
The MFDP, in partnership with the Ministry of Internal Affairs and supported by various partners, conducted consultations across all 73 districts in the country. These consultations were followed by county-level discussions and the validation of input from local communities. The National Steering Committee on the National Development Plan (NDP) was formed, and dialogues with UN experts were held to align the NDP with the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) for 2030.
Preparations are underway for the formal launch of the NDP in January 2025. Additionally, the Public Sector Investment Plan and County Development Agendas have been drafted, with the support of two Liberian think tanks leading the efforts.
Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC):
The Ministry of Finance and Development Planning (MFDP) played a crucial role in the successful negotiations that enabled the government of Liberia to secure the Millennium Challenge Corporation (MCC) Compact. This achievement marks a significant milestone for the country, as it opens up new opportunities for development and progress. Through careful negotiations and strategic efforts, the MFDP ensured that Liberia would benefit from the resources and support provided by the MCC, fostering economic growth and improving key sectors within the nation.

a3097.t:
Monrovia, Liberia; August 13, 2025 — In a powerful opening statement at the city dialogue titled “Improving Monrovia City Administration through Effective Leadership, Proper Coordination, and Resource Mobilization,” the Mayor of Monrovia, John S. Siafa, has issued a clarion call for sweeping reforms to rescue Liberia’s capital from decades of administrative fragmentation and fiscal dependency.
Mayor Siafa began by invoking Monrovia’s historic legacy, tracing its roots to 1822 when it was founded as Christopolis and later renamed in honor of late U.S. President James Monroe. Despite its status as Liberia’s political and economic heart, the Mayor lamented that Monrovia remains hamstrung by outdated laws, overlapping authorities, and weak institutional coordination.
He highlighted legal and administrative confusion stemming from multiple acts and agencies governing Monrovia and its surrounding districts. From the 1922 Commonwealth Act to the 1973 City Government Act, and the creation of townships like Congo Town and New Kru Town, the lack of clear boundaries and service mandates has led to duplication and inefficiency.
The mayor pointed to the erosion of the Monrovia City Corporation’s (MCC) original mandates, such as zoning and land use—which have been absorbed by newer national agencies like the Ministry of Public Works (MPW) and the Liberia Land Authority (LLA), without corresponding legal reforms.
Mayor Siafa outlined five critical issues undermining Monrovia’s development: Unclear jurisdictional boundaries, causing disputes and wasted resources—fragmented governance, with no metropolitan body to align city and national efforts. Erosion of MCC’s mandates in zoning and development regulations. Fiscal dependency on central government subsidies.Regulatory gaps, weakening enforcement and livability standards.
He warned that these challenges have led to unplanned urban sprawl, deteriorating infrastructure, and the expansion of informal settlements. Fiscal fragmentation, he emphasized, is particularly damaging, leaving MCC unable to respond to population growth or invest in public services.
To reverse Monrovia’s decline, he proposed a bold reform agenda that includes establishing a Permanent Metropolitan Coordination Body to unify city and national agencies; reforming the MCC Act to clarify mandates and eliminate overlaps; implementing fiscal reforms to increase local revenue generation and reduce dependency; integrating service delivery frameworks with clear roles and oversight; and strengthening regulatory enforcement to attract investment and improve urban standards.
Calling this a defining moment for Monrovia, Mayor Siafa concluded with a passionate appeal for action: “The urgency cannot be overstated. Monrovia’s future will be determined by the choices we make now—whether we allow fragmentation and dependency to persist, or whether we commit to decisive reforms that secure strong governance, fiscal independence, and integrated service delivery.”

a3287.t:
By Thokozani Mazibuko 
The Minister of Education and Training, Owen Nxumalo, has hailed Macmillan Education Eswatini as a key partner in the country’s journey toward delivering quality and culturally relevant education, describing the company’s contributions as a cornerstone of Eswatini’s educational transformation.
The Minister made these remarks on Monday during his official visit to Macmillan Publishers’ premises in Matsapha, where he met with management and staff to assess the company’s ongoing collaboration with the Ministry in supporting curriculum development, textbook production, and digital learning initiatives.
“It is a great honour to be here today on this official visit to Macmillan Education Eswatini, a valued partner in our national journey to deliver quality education to all Emaswati,” Nxumalo said.
“This visit is not only an opportunity to engage with our longest-standing partners but also to reflect on the impact of our shared efforts and look towards the future with renewed courage.”
Education and Industry: A partnership for National growth
Nxumalo noted that Macmillan’s location in Matsapha Eswatini’s industrial hub symbolized the interconnection between education and economic development. He commended the company for not only producing high-quality educational materials but also contributing to the local economy by supporting small businesses and entrepreneurs.		
		
“I was pleased to learn that, over and above providing quality educational materials, the company supports local entrepreneurs by procuring from them and ensuring they are paid before their due invoice dates,” the Minister highlighted.
“By publishing high-quality educational resources, Macmillan has helped develop a skilled workforce and seasoned entrepreneurs.
This contribution has supported the rise of enterprises that depend on a literate and capable population, showing how education and industry can work hand in hand to drive national progress.”
A transformative partnership rooted in history
Reflecting on the history of Eswatini’s education system, Nxumalo celebrated what he termed one of the most “transformative partnerships in the history of education” the collaboration between the Government of Eswatini and Macmillan Publishers.
He traced the roots of this partnership back to the mid-1970s, when the Government made a bold decision to end reliance on imported textbooks from apartheid-era South Africa and instead develop materials that reflected Eswatini’s values, language, and aspirations.
“Before 1978, all primary school textbooks used in Eswatini were imported from South Africa, reflecting the apartheid-era Bantu Education system a system foreign to our values, our culture, and our aspirations as an independent nation,” Nxumalo explained.
Between 1974 and 1977, with support from the World Bank, USAID, and universities in the United States, up to 40 Swati curriculum specialists were trained to design and develop Eswatini’s first national curriculum.
The result was the establishment of the Primary Curriculum Unit, now known as the National Curriculum Centre (NCC) in Manzini.
“By 1977, the NCC had successfully developed the first textbooks for Grades 1 and 2 in English, Mathematics, SiSwati, and Science. This was a defining moment the birth of an education system built by emaSwati, for emaSwati,” the Minister said proudly.
Nxumalo lauded the role of His late Majesty King Sobhuza II in facilitating a groundbreaking partnership between the Government and Macmillan one that was later recognized globally as a model public–private partnership for developing nations.
Under His Majesty’s visionary leadership, Macmillan’s Southern African headquarters were relocated from Johannesburg to Matsapha, establishing Macmillan BOLESWA Publishers and the Macmillan Swaziland National Publishing Company (MSNP).
This collaboration produced not only textbooks but an entire ecosystem of educational publishing that empowered local authors, illustrators, and curriculum experts.
“Importantly, all textbooks used in our primary schools today are written and developed by Eswatini’s own curriculum designers,” Nxumalo emphasized.
Driving digital transformation
The Minister also praised Macmillan for embracing innovation by supporting the Ministry’s blended learning project, which utilizes the company’s digital platform to deliver 21st Century teaching and learning.
The pilot project began in 2022 with two public schools and a cohort of Grade 4 learners, who are now part of a digital learning transformation that is expected to expand nationwide in the coming years.
Nxumalo said the Ministry remains committed to building on this legacy as the country transitions toward Competency-Based Education and digital learning models.
He encouraged Macmillan and other publishers to continue playing an active role in shaping the next phase of educational reform.
“The future of this nation is great, especially as we work together to deliver the most prized asset that any nation can possess a well-educated and empowered generation,” he said.
“As we navigate the realities of a rapidly changing world, His Majesty’s Government will continue to seek out innovative ideas from publishers such as Macmillan. Your creativity and strategic foresight are essential in preparing our learners for the future.”
Nxumalo concluded by expressing deep appreciation to Macmillan Education Eswatini for its unwavering support and investment in the country’s education system.
“Let me express our deepest appreciation to Macmillan Education Eswatini for its dedication to the development of our nation. May this partnership continue to flourish,” he said.

a3375.t:
Mali : opération militaire d’envergure à Sébabougou
L’intervention militaire de ce lundi à Sébabiugou, dans la région de Nioro du Sahel, visait à restaurer l’ordre public, assurer la protection des civils et permettre le retour progressif des populations déplacées.
Depuis fin 2024, la localité de Sébabougou vivait sous embargo. Les groupes armés, désorganisés mais encore actifs, empêchaient toute circulation de biens, de personnes et d’aide humanitaire. Les habitants, soumis à des pressions croissantes, avaient en grande partie été contraints de fuir vers les communes voisines, aggravant la situation humanitaire dans cette partie du Sahel malien.
L’opération militaire, déclenchée par les FAMa dans la matinée du 28 avril, a permis de reprendre le contrôle de la localité en début d’après-midi. Lors de leur progression, les unités ont violemment déjoué une embuscade tendue par les terroristes, puis consolidé leur avancée par des frappes aériennes ciblées contre des bases de repli situées dans les forêts environnantes.
Le bilan provisoire communiqué par l’état-major général des armées fait état de cinq soldats blessés, pris en charge par les services médicaux, et de vingt-et-un terroristes neutralisés. Une quantité importante de matériel militaire, de moyens de communication, de véhicules et de logistique a été récupérée dans la localité. Les frappes aériennes ont également détruit plusieurs retranchements ennemis.
Cette action militaire s’inscrit dans une dynamique offensive engagée entre le 11 et le 15 avril, au cours de laquelle plusieurs bases terroristes avaient été démantelées dans les secteurs de Sébabougou, Gomitira, Wataye, Forêt de Tongui, Niamakoro, Kouloufladiengué, Fadiabougou, Donibabougou, Douala, Nelou, Sirado et Kwala. Malgré ces succès militaires, des groupes armés avaient continué à harceler les populations civiles de Sébabougou, cherchant à imposer leur autorité par la violence et l’intimidation.
Selon des témoignages recueillis par des sources locales fiables et recoupés par plusieurs médias maliens, les conditions de vie dans Sébabougou étaient devenues extrêmement précaires : coupures d’approvisionnement, restrictions de mouvement, violences et menaces constantes. L’intervention des FAMa, au-delà de sa dimension militaire, représente ainsi une réponse à une urgence humanitaire criante.
L’état-major général des armées a assuré que toutes les mesures seront prises pour sécuriser durablement la zone, protéger les civils, faciliter la libre circulation et empêcher toute tentative de réimplantation des groupes armés dans la région. Une surveillance renforcée a été mise en place autour de Sébabougou et dans les secteurs environnants.
Dans son communiqué, l’état-major a rendu hommage au professionnalisme et au courage des soldats engagés, tout en soulignant que la lutte pour la stabilisation du centre et du nord du Mali nécessite une action constante et déterminée.
MD/ac/Sf/APA

a3375.en:
Mali: large-scale military operation at Sebabougou

Monday's military intervention at Sebabougou, in the Nioro du Sahel region, was aimed at restoring public order, ensuring the protection of civilians and permitting the gradual return of displaced populations.

Since the end of 2024, the locality of Sebabougou had been living under embargo. The armed groups, disorganised but still active, were preventing any movement of goods, people and humanitarian aid. The inhabitants, subjected to growing pressure, had largely been forced to flee to neighbouring communes, aggravating the humanitarian situation in this part of the Malian Sahel.

The military operation, launched by the FAMa (Malian Armed Forces) on the morning of 28 April, made it possible to retake control of the locality in the early afternoon. During their advance, the units violently foiled an ambush laid by the terrorists, then consolidated their advance with targeted air strikes against fallback bases located in the surrounding forests.

The provisional toll communicated by the general staff of the armed forces reports five soldiers wounded, treated by the medical services, and twenty-one terrorists neutralised. A significant quantity of military equipment, communications equipment, vehicles and logistics was recovered in the locality. The air strikes also destroyed several enemy entrenchments.

This military action is part of an offensive dynamic launched between 11 and 15 April, during which several terrorist bases had been dismantled in the sectors of Sebabougou, Gomitira, Wataye, the Tongui Forest, Niamakoro, Kouloufladiengue, Fadiabougou, Donibabougou, Douala, Nelou, Sirado and Kwala. Despite these military successes, armed groups had continued to harass the civilian population of Sebabougou, seeking to impose their authority through violence and intimidation.

According to testimonies gathered by reliable local sources and cross-checked by several Malian media outlets, living conditions in Sebabougou had become extremely precarious: supply cut-offs, restrictions on movement, violence and constant threats. The FAMa intervention, beyond its military dimension, thus represents a response to a glaring humanitarian emergency.

The general staff of the armed forces gave assurances that all measures will be taken to secure the zone durably, protect civilians, facilitate free movement and prevent any attempt by the armed groups to re-establish themselves in the region. Reinforced surveillance has been put in place around Sebabougou and in the surrounding sectors.

In its communique, the general staff paid tribute to the professionalism and courage of the soldiers engaged, while stressing that the struggle for the stabilisation of central and northern Mali requires constant and determined action.

MD/ac/Sf/APA

a3537.t:
The Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation has called for enhanced bilateral ties and cooperation between South Sudan and Germany in areas of capacity building, agriculture, education and technology, among others.
Amb. Monday Semaya also called on the German government to boost its investment in South Sudan particularly in trade through the establishment of a joint cooperation commission.
He also encourages Berlin to support South Sudan’s transition to lasting peace through the implementation of the 2018 peace agreement and the country’s ambition for economic reforms.
In a speech during German Unity Day, Semaya further commended the European nation for being one of the first countries in the world to recognize the independence of South Sudan on July 9, 2011.
“We look forward for more cooperation, particularly in the areas of capacity building, agriculture, education, technology, cultural exchanges and trade investment, including support for the peace process in South Sudan,” he said.
“I and my government believe that we can achieve more positive and encouraging results through establishment of a joint bilateral commission, and other reliable and practical bilateral engagement.”
Amb. Semaya further appreciated the government of Germany for its humanitarian efforts, including the contribution of its police to the UN peacekeeping mission in South Sudan.
The German government is providing humanitarian assistance in South Sudan, as one of the biggest donors supporting refugees and other displaced populations with emergency food aid, and protective and hygiene measures.

Monrovia, Liberia; August 21, 2025 – The Governance Commission, in collaboration with the Ministries of Internal Affairs, Finance, and Development Planning, has ended a two-day policy dialogue aimed at strengthening coordination of the Monrovia City Corporation.
The two-day brainstorming gathering held under the theme “Improving Monrovia City Administration through Effective Leadership, Proper Coordination, and Resource Mobilization” captured strategy on mobilizing resources and the adoption of several recommendations.
The policy dialogue brought together representatives from the MCC, the Governance Commission, and the Ministry of Internal Affairs, among many others.
Speaking at the program marking the end of the dialogue, Governance Commission Acting Chairman, Professor Alaric Togba, stressed the need for the authority to demarcate Monrovia and provide its statutory mandates.
Professor Togba disclosed that participants have agreed that there is an urgent need to review the mandates of institutions that have similar mandates to the Monrovia City Corporation
The participants agreed on the importance of political and administrative reorganization of Monrovia City to align with other cities in international best practices.
During the two days, concerns were raised about the duplication of functions, service delivery gaps, unclear jurisdictions, fragmented governance, revenue collection disputes, erosion of mandates, and overlap of administrative boundaries.
Other concerns included legal inconsistencies, weak regulatory enforcement mechanisms, the use of electoral districts as administrative districts, and the recentralization of decentralization.
According to Professor Togba, the Governance Commission considers that participants at the two-day policy dialogue reached the understanding that there is a pressing need for the political and administrative reorganization of Monrovia.
He encouraged leaders and stakeholder engagements on actionable steps regarding the way forward.
Professor Togba also stressed the imperative for concrete agreements and decision-making processes on what needs to be done to improve Monrovia City and make it a better and safer place for future generations.
“Clearly, there are disturbing ambiguities and conflicting ideas about the demarcation of Monrovia that require authoritative clarification.
Undeniably, addressing the foundational challenges we face will require a review of the constitution of Liberia and a review of the mandates and functions of institutions and agencies that have roles and responsibilities for managing affairs and providing services in Monrovia city,” he added.
Professor Togba rallies stakeholders’ efforts in reconciling the overlaps and conflicts between institutional mandates concerned with the administration of Monrovia.
He pointed out that the city government of Monrovia needs to be reorganized, properly coordinated, and better monetized for the promotion of development.
The Governance Commission also pointed to the lack of knowledge and understanding as a national issue that can no longer be ignored and emphasized that public education and awareness demand the reintroduction of the teaching of government and civics in the schools. Editing by Jonathan Browne

Niamey, 12 nov (ANP-WAM) – Le président des Émirats arabes unis, Son Altesse Cheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, a publié un décret fédéral portant création de l’Agence d’aide internationale des Émirats arabes unis affiliée au Conseil international des affaires humanitaires. Elle jouit d’une identité juridique indépendante et d’une pleine capacité d’action.
Cette Agence est chargée de mettre en œuvre les programmes d’aide étrangère à la lumière de la politique générale des affaires humanitaires internationales, ainsi que de planifier, de superviser, de mettre en œuvre et de suivre le soutien officiel du gouvernement, les projets et les initiatives de développement, les programmes de redressement rapide et de réinstallation, et de mettre en œuvre les plans d’intervention humanitaire et de secours.
Son Altesse Cheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, vice-président et vice-premier ministre des Émirats arabes unis et président de la Cour présidentielle, a souligné que la fondation de l’Agence d’aide internationale des Émirats arabes unis s’inscrivait dans le prolongement de l’approche humanitaire établie par le père fondateur, feu Cheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan.
Pour lui cette approche reflète l’engagement des Émirats arabes unis à relever les défis humanitaires et à promouvoir le développement durable au niveau mondial.
» Les Émirats arabes unis poursuivent cette voie sous la direction avisée et le soutien continu de Son Altesse Cheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, président des Émirats arabes unis, ce qui confirme l’engagement des dirigeants, du gouvernement et du peuple à promouvoir cette noble voie humanitaire « , a déclaré Son Altesse.
De son côté, Son Altesse Cheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, vice-premier ministre et ministre des Affaires étrangères, a expliqué que la création de l’Agence d’aide internationale des Émirats arabes unis est une affirmation du rôle central et continu des Émirats arabes unis dans la fourniture d’une aide vitale, dans l’amélioration des conditions de vie et dans le soutien aux communautés et aux peuples sur tous les continents.
Son Altesse a souligné la volonté des Émirats arabes unis à travailler côte à côte avec des partenaires internationaux afin d’orienter les efforts conjoints vers la création d’un changement et d’un impact positifs tangibles et durables, en particulier dans les régions qui souffrent de crises et d’instabilité, en se concentrant sur les domaines de la vie de base tels que les services éducatifs, les installations de santé et les secteurs d’infrastructure dans le but de parvenir au développement et à la prospérité pour les peuples.
Pour sa part, Son Altesse Cheikh Theyab bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, vice-président de la Cour présidentielle pour les affaires de développement et les familles des martyrs et président du Conseil international des affaires humanitaires, a souligné que la création de l’Agence d’aide internationale des Émirats arabes unis est une amélioration de l’action humanitaire pionnière des Émirats arabes unis dans le monde.
Cheikh Theyab de souligner que l’Agence vise à continuer à enrichir l’aide étrangère de priorité mondiale et à maximiser ses effets positifs dans la mise en œuvre de programmes d’aide humanitaire, d’initiatives et de projets de développement dans diverses régions du monde, conformément au rôle et à la position des Émirats arabes unis dans le travail humanitaire et de développement aux niveaux régional et international.
Les Émirats arabes unis sont au premier rang des pays donateurs dans le monde, puisque les rapports officiels et les chiffres enregistrés montrent que depuis leur création par feu Cheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan, les Émirats arabes unis ont fourni plus de 360 milliards AED (98 milliards USD) d’aide étrangère dans divers domaines humanitaires et secteurs de développement, au profit de plus d’un milliard de personnes dans différentes parties et régions du monde.
WAM-ANP 044 novembre 2024
a3800.en:
Niamey, 12 Nov (ANP-WAM) - The President of the United Arab Emirates, His Highness Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, has issued a federal decree establishing the United Arab Emirates International Aid Agency, affiliated with the International Humanitarian and Charity Council. It enjoys an independent legal identity and full capacity to act.
This Agency is responsible for implementing foreign aid programmes in light of the general policy on international humanitarian affairs, as well as for planning, supervising, implementing and monitoring official government support, development projects and initiatives, rapid recovery and resettlement programmes, and for implementing humanitarian and relief response plans.
His Highness Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Vice-President and Deputy Prime Minister of the United Arab Emirates and Chairman of the Presidential Court, stressed that the founding of the United Arab Emirates International Aid Agency was a continuation of the humanitarian approach established by the founding father, the late Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan.
For him, this approach reflects the commitment of the United Arab Emirates to meeting humanitarian challenges and promoting sustainable development at the global level.
"The United Arab Emirates pursues this path under the wise leadership and continued support of His Highness Sheikh Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, President of the United Arab Emirates, which confirms the commitment of the leadership, the government and the people to promoting this noble humanitarian path," His Highness declared.
For his part, His Highness Sheikh Abdullah bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, explained that the creation of the United Arab Emirates International Aid Agency is an affirmation of the central and continuing role of the United Arab Emirates in providing vital aid, in improving living conditions and in supporting communities and peoples on all continents.
His Highness underlined the willingness of the United Arab Emirates to work side by side with international partners in order to direct joint efforts towards the creation of tangible and lasting positive change and impact, particularly in regions suffering from crises and instability, focusing on basic areas of life such as educational services, health facilities and infrastructure sectors with the aim of achieving development and prosperity for peoples.
For his part, His Highness Sheikh Theyab bin Mohamed bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Deputy Chairman of the Presidential Court for Development Affairs and Families of Martyrs and Chairman of the International Humanitarian and Charity Council, stressed that the creation of the United Arab Emirates International Aid Agency is an enhancement of the pioneering humanitarian action of the United Arab Emirates in the world.
Sheikh Theyab stressed that the Agency aims to continue to enrich foreign aid of global priority and to maximize its positive effects in the implementation of humanitarian aid programmes, initiatives and development projects in various regions of the world, in keeping with the role and position of the United Arab Emirates in humanitarian and development work at the regional and international levels.
The United Arab Emirates are at the forefront of donor countries in the world, since official reports and recorded figures show that since their founding by the late Sheikh Zayed bin Sultan Al Nahyan, the United Arab Emirates have provided more than 360 billion AED (98 billion USD) in foreign aid in various humanitarian fields and development sectors, benefiting more than one billion people in different parts and regions of the world.
WAM-ANP 044 November 2024

a3816.t:
The government has signed a $16 million financing agreement with the African Development Bank (AfDB) for implementation of three projects including water and hygiene, floods response, and youth and women empowerment.
The grant will be channeled to World Food Program and UN Development Fund and will include support for youth and women through small and medium enterprises, and humanitarian assistance for flood-affected communities and refugees.
The Minister of Finance and Planning Dr. Marial Dongrin signed on behalf of the government and Themba Bhebhe signed on behalf of the African Development Bank.
WFP Resident Representative Dr. Mohamed Abchir, said the initiatives are significant in creating jobs, fostering entrepreneurship, and building resilience among South Sudanese youth and women.
He noted the impact of previous initiatives supported by the AfDB and emphasizes the importance of investing in local agriculture and job creation to reduce humanitarian needs.
“The objective of this job creation program using the small and medium enterprises is also to build the resilience of the population,” said Dr. Abchir.
“We see more and more program now coming through that window of resilience building and development which are really quite important here in South Sudan.”
“We’ve seen some of the impact and the results of previous programs supported by the African Development Bank and we are going to build on the results but also on the lessons learned from that previous support.”
The African Development Bank Country Manager, Themba Bhebhe, revealed that a future $10.6 million grant would go toward improving water and sanitation services, a critical need in Juba and other areas.
This project will be implemented by the South Sudan Urban Water Corporation to upgrade sanitation systems and ensure access to clean drinking water.
“Today we are signing three operations as my colleagues have said. The water and sanitation one is 10.6 million, the women and youth is about 5.4 million and about 500,000 grant which WFP would administer,” he explained.
“So this is about 16 million that we are signing today. But our plan, probably as you are aware Minister, for the first time the Bank has approved seven projects in one year.”
Bhebhe also announced the AfDB’s approval of a $200 million energy project, including a 300-kilometer transmission line to import electricity from Uganda.
This initiative aims to reduce South Sudan’s high electricity tariffs, which are among the highest in the region, and improve energy access.
Meanwhile, the Minister of Humanitarian Affairs Albino Atak expressed gratitude to development partners for their response to the humanitarian crisis caused by floods and the influx of refugees from Sudan.
“This year, the floods have affected about 1.4 million people and displaced almost 400,000 people. And the effects of floods are still there up to now.”
“We are even struggling now to respond to them but also to respond to recovery. Recovery process is difficult. So with the presence of developmental partners I think we will also be able to put something for recovery.”
The projects are expected to enhance livelihoods, improve infrastructure, and provide much-needed support to vulnerable communities, marking a significant step forward in South Sudan’s journey toward resilience and sustainable development.
