a4675.t:
The first commercial flight in Syria since the toppling of longtime President Bashar al-Assad earlier this month has taken off from Damascus airport.
The flight landed in Aleppo, in the country’s north, on Wednesday with 43 people on board including a group of journalists.
Pro-Assad forces abandoned the airport in the capital on December 8 as opposition fighters closed in on the city following a lightning offensive that began on November 27. Since then, no flights had taken off or landed due to security reasons.
Earlier this week, airport staff painted the pro-opposition three-star flag on aeroplanes, a symbol of the 2011 uprising now adopted by the transitional authorities. Inside the terminal, the new flag has also replaced the one associated with the government of al-Assad, who fled to Russia.
An airport official told the AFP news agency on condition of anonymity that international flights would resume on December 24, following maintenance work.
Meanwhile, neighbouring Jordan has reopened the Jaber border crossing with for trade, resuming the flow of goods and freight traffic between the two countries.
More than 13 years after a brutal crackdown on antigovernment protests morphed into a multisided war that killed hundreds of thousands and displaced millions, Syria is struggling to get back on its feet as it comes to terms with the scars of torture, disappearances and summary executions.
The group at the helm of Syria’s new ruling coalition, Hayat Tahrir al-Sham (HTS), has sought to keep its institutions going and kickstart its economy. Once rooted in Syria’s branch of al-Qaeda and designated a “terrorist” organisation by several Western governments, HTS has softened its rhetoric and pledged to protect the nation’s diverse religious and ethnic communities.
While the new caretaker administration in Damascus has set out few details on its thinking for the next steps for the country, newly appointed Prime Minister Mohammed al-Bashir, who formerly led an HTS-affiliated government in Idlib province, has said he will remain in office until March.
‘Free and fair elections’
On Wednesday, a day after meeting HTS leader Ahmed al-Sharaa in Damascus, United Nations Special Envoy Geir Pedersen called for “free and fair elections” in Syria after the transition and urgent humanitarian assistance for the country.
Pedersen, who on Tuesday warned that the war has not yet ended, told reporters in Damascus that “there is a lot of hope that we can now see the beginning of a new Syria”.
He also expressed hope for a “political solution” in the Kurdish-held northeast, where the US-backed, Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF) are battling Turkish-backed groups who have captured several Kurdish towns since the offensive began in the rest of the country last month.
Speaking to AFP, HTS military chief Murhaf Abu Qasra said Kurdish-held areas would be integrated under the country’s new leadership, adding that the group rejects federalism and that “Syria will not be divided.”
“The Kurdish people are one of the components of the Syrian people … Syria will not be divided and there will be no federal entities,” he said.
Abu Qasra, known by his nom de guerre Abu Hassan al-Hamawi, also said the group would be “the first” to dissolve its armed wing and integrate into the armed forces.
Meanwhile, Hadi al-Bahra, head of the Syrian National Coalition that grouped opponents of al-Assad during the war, said on Wednesday that Syria’s transitional government should be credible and not exclude any Syrian party or be based on sectarianism.
The Turkiye-based Syrian National Coalition would return to Syria and set up headquarters there, al-Bahra told journalists at a news briefing, adding that he intended to return as well.
“Logistics should be worked out and freedom of speech should be guaranteed,” he added.
His comments came a day after members of the UN Security Council in a statement called for the implementation of “an inclusive and Syrian-led and Syrian-owned political process” that they said should meet the legitimate aspirations of all Syrians, protect all of them and “enable them to peacefully, independently and democratically determine their own futures”.
The 15-member body also emphasised battling “terrorism” across the country, stressing that Syria must abide by council resolutions on non-conventional weapons and reiterating support for UN peacekeepers and the inviolability of diplomatic premises.

a4808.t:
THE government has disclosed that collaborating partners and some financial institutions have shown interest to develop the livestock and fisheries sectors in the country.
Minister of Agriculture and Cooperatives, in-charge of livestock and
fisheries, Bradford Machila said support in infrastructure development, camp house rehabilitation and laboratory construction in the two sectors will improve Zambia’s economy.
Mr Machila named the financial institutions that have pledged to
support the livestock and the fisheries sectors as the African
Development Development and the World Bank.
He said the other collaborating partnership, such as the European
Union, Common Market for Eastern Southern African Countries (COMESA),
USAID and the Southern African Development Committee (SADC) have also
shown willingness to support Zambia in the fisheries and livestock
sectors.
The minister said was speaking when he addressed district heads and provincial heads of government departments in Namwala district of southern province.
Mr Machila stated that the new ministry of livestock and fisheries expected to be established is committed to deliver better services to the country that will enhance economic development.
He noted that government’s commitment to ensure development in the two
sectors has been evidenced by increased funding allocated to the
two sectors.
‘’Government is in a hurry to develop the livestock and fisheries
sectors and we should all apply ourselves diligently to meet the
objectives and targets in the newly established ministry of
agriculture and cooperatives in livestock and fisheries,’’ he noted.
Mr Machila clarified that government has prioritized the disease
control programme in the livestock sector before lifting the livestock
movement ban.
He noted that the ministry will focus on prevention of diseases than
control.
Mr Machila also noted that control measures of diseases will still be
undertaken but emphasized that it was better to prevent the diseases.
He, however, regretted the inconvenience that might have been caused to
farmers by instituting a livestock ban but maintained that government
was taking disease prevention and control by putting in place a
movement ban of animals as a matter of urgency and high priority.
The minister said that vaccination programmes against diseases will be
continued by the veterinary department to curb animal diseases.
ZANIS-NAIS/ENDS/LK/EB

a4864.t:
- በጉባዔው በበይነ መረብ የተሳተፉ ጥያቄ ተነስቶባቸዋል
- ክለቡ ከ163 ሚሊዮን ብር በላይ ዕዳ አለበት ተብሏል
ከተመሠረተ አንድ ክፍለ ዘመን ሊደፍን ከጫፍ የደረሰው አንጋፋው የቅዱስ ጊዮርጊስ ስፖርት ማኅበር፣ ከስድስት ዓመታት በኋላ፣ በቅሎ ቤት በሚገኘው ኢትዮጵያ ሆቴል (ግሎባል) ለመጀመሪያ ጊዜ ባካሄደው ጠቅላላ ጉባዔ የክለቡን የቦርድ አመራሮች መርጧል፡፡ ጥቅምት 16 ቀን 2018 ዓ.ም. የተጠራውን ጠቅላላ ጉባዔ ለመታደም ሪፖርተር በሥፍራው በተገኘበት ወቅትም፣ ሆቴሉ በፀጥታ ኃይሎች ከፍተኛ ጥበቃ መኖሩን አስተውሏል፡፡ ጉባዔው በተደረገበት አዳራሹ ውስጥ ደግሞ ጠንከር ጠንከር ያለ ተክለ ሰውነት ያላቸው ሰዎች ፈንጠር ፈንጠር ብለው ቆመው ጉባዔውን ሲከታሉ እንደነበርም ታዝቧል፡፡
ጉባዔው የተጀመረው የስፖርት ማኅበሩ ደጋፊዎች በመታወቂያ እየተለዩ ወደ አዳራሹ እንዲገቡ ከተደረገ በኋላ ነበር፡፡ ጉባዔው በይፋ መጀመሩን ያበሰሩት ደግሞ የቦርዱ ዋና ጸሐፊ አቶ ነዋይ በየነ ሲሆኑ፣ ሌሎች የቦርድ አመራሮች ያልተገኙበት ምክንያት ግን አልተገለጸም፡፡ በሕይወት የሌሉ የቦርድ አመራሮችን ጨምሮ ለሌሎችም ባለውለተኞች የአንድ ደቂቃ የህሊና ጸሎት ተደርጓል፡፡ ቀጥሎ የስፖርት ማኅበሩ ያለፉት አምስት ዓመታት የዕቅድ ክንውን ከቀረበ በኋላ፣ በገለልተኛ የሒሳብ ባለሙያ የኦዲት ሪፖርትም ቀርቧል፡፡
ለጉባዔው በቀረበው የኦዲት ሪፖርት መሠረት ክለቡ በዚህ ጊዜ ያለው የተጣራ ሀብት 13,010,692 ብር መሆኑ፣ ለዚህም ስፖርት ማኅበሩ በተለይም ባለፉት አምስት ዓመታት ከአጋር ድርጅቶች ማግኘት የነበረበት ገቢ በእጅጉ እያሽቆለቆለ መምጣቱ በሪፖርቱ ተጠቅሷል፡፡
በሒደቱ የተጫዋቾችና የሠራተኞች የደመወዝ ክፍያ መዘግየት ማጋጠሙ፣ በተጨማሪም ስፖርት ማኅበሩ በዚህ ጊዜ ለአግልግሎት ሰጪ ተቋማት፣ እንዲሁም የደመወዝ ግብርና ጡረታ ያልተከፈለ 163,832,000 ብር ዕዳ እንዳለበትም ተነግሯል፡፡ ከዕዳው 22 ሚሊዮን ብር ለክለቡ ፕሬዚዳንት አቶ አብነት ገብረ መስቀል መከፈል የነበረበት መሆኑም በሪፖርቱ ተጠቅሷል፡፡ ከአጋር ድርጅቶች ያልተሰበሰበ ተብሎ የቀረበው 41 ሚሊዮን ብር እንዳለም በኦዲት ሪፖርቱ ተካቷል፡፡
የዕቅድ ክንውኑን በተመለከተ ከቀረበው ሪፖርት መካከል የኢትዮጵያ ፕሪሚየር ሊግ ከኮቪድ-19 ወረርሽኝ በኋላ፣ በተወሰኑ ከተሞች ብቻ እንዲካሄድ መደረጉ የክለቡን ፋይናንስ በእጅጉ እንዳናጋው፣ ይህም ሆኖ ስፖርት ማኅበሩ በለሚ ኩራ ክፍለ ከተማ 10 ሺሕ ካሬ ሜትር ቦታ ተረክቦ እንደነበር በሪፖርቱ ተካቷል፡፡ ከመሬቱ በኮሪደር ልማት ምክንያት ሁለት ሺሕ ካሬ ሜትር ቦታ ተወስዶበት፣ አዲስ ካርታ (የይዞታ ማረጋገጫ) ለመቀበል እየተጠባበቀ ይገኛልም ተብሏል፡፡
በቢሾፍቱ ከተማ የተሠራው የክቡር ይድነቃቸው ተሰማ አካዴሚ አሁን ላይ የዋናው ቡድን ካምፕ (መኖሪያ) ሆኖ እያገለገለ እንደሚገኝ፣ አካዴሚው ጉዳት እንዳይደርስበት ለግል ድርጅቶች ተሰጥቶ ክትትል እንዲደረግለት ስለመደረጉ ጭምር በሪፖርቱ ቀርቧል፡፡ ሪፖርቱ እየቀረበ በሚገኝበት ወቅት ለወትሮው፣ ‹‹አንድ ክለብ አንድ ቤተሰብ›› በሚል የሚታወቁት የክለቡ ደጋፊዎች ለሁለት ተከፍለው ታይተዋል፡፡
ጉባዔው በዕቅድ ክንውኑና በኦዲት ሪፖርቱ ዙሪያ አስተያየት እንዲሰጥበት ከመደረጉ በፊት፣ የክለቡን ቦርድ ለረዥም ዓመታት በሰብሳቢነት የመሩት አቶ አብነት ገብረ መስቀል በበይነ መረብ አማካይነት በስፖርት ማኅበሩ ወቅታዊ ጉዳዮች ዙሪያ ሪፖርት አቅርበዋል፡፡
ጉባዔውን በታዛቢነት እንዲከታተል በሥፍራው የነበረው የኢትዮጵያ እግር ኳስ ፌዴሬሽን የጉባዔውን አካሄድ፣ በተለይም ከመመርያና ደንብ አኳያ አስተያየት እንዲሰጥ ከመድረኩ ዕድል አግኝቶ፣ ‹‹የስፖርት ማኅበሩ መተዳደሪያ ደንብ በበይነ መረብ አማካይነት ሪፖርት ማቅረብ ይቻላል ወይ?›› የሚል ጥያቄ ካቀረበ በኋላም ጉባዔው እንዲቀጥል ተደርጓል፡፡
መድረኩ የዕቅድ ክንውኑና የኦዲት ሪፖርቱ በድምፅ እንዲፀድቅ ከማስደረጉ አስቀድሞ፣ ከጉባዔው አባላት አስተያየት እንዲሰጥበት ፈቅዷል፡፡ ይህንን ተከትሎ በርከት ያሉ እጆች ከፍ ብለው ነበር የታዩት፡፡ የመናገር ዕድል ካገኙት እጆች ጥቂት የማይባሉት አስተያየቶች፣ ‹‹የቀረበው ሪፖርት የሚያመላክተው አንጋፋው የቅዱስ ጊዮርጊስ ስፖርት ማኅበር በአሁኑ ወቅት በከባድ የህልውና ፈተና ውስጥ መሆኑን ነው፡፡ ለዚህ ሁሉ ችግር በሕግ አግባብ በየዓመቱ መካሄድ የነበረበት ጠቅላላ ጉባዔ እንዲካሄድ አለማድረግ፣ ለዚህ ደግሞ በዚህ ጉባዔ ላይ የአገልግሎት ጊዜውን ጨርሷል፡፡ ለዚህም ሕጋዊ አካል መሰየም ያስፈልጋል፡፡ አካል የነበረው ሁኔታ በገለልተኛ አካል ሳይጣራ ምርጫ ማድረግ ተገቢም ሕጋዊም አይደለም፤›› የሚለውም ይጠቀሳል፡፡
በተለይም ‹‹የአምስት ዓመት ተብሎ ሊቀርብ የቻለው የኦዲት ሪፖርት በየዓመቱ ጠቅላላ ጉባዔ ላይ ቀርቦ ሳይፀድቅና አስተያየት ሳይሰጥበት የአምስት ዓመት ተብሎ የኦዲት ሪፖርት ተብሎ እንዴት ነው ሊቀርብ የሚችለው? ከአጋር ድርጅቶች ያልተሰበሰበ ተብሎ የቀረበው 41 ሚሊዮን ብር የኦዲት ግኝት መጀመሪያ ስምምነት ሲደረግ በሕግና ሕግ ላይ የተመሠረተ አልነበረም ማለት ነውን? ከሆነስ ለምን ጉዳዩን በሕግ አግባብ መከታተልና ማስፈጸም አልተቻለም? የስፖርት ማኅበሩ ክበብ እንቅስቃሴ በኦዲት ሪፖርቱ አልተካተተም፣ ለምን?›› በሚል ከሁሉም አቅጣጫ ጥያቄው እየበረታ ሲመጣ፣ በተለይም ከመድረኩ አዝማሚያውን ለማስቆም የተሄደበት መንገድ ጉባዔው ለሁለት እንዲከፈልና አላስፈላጊ ንትርክ እንዲፈጠር ምክንያት ሆኖም ነበር፡፡
ከመድረኩ ‹‹አስተያየት ይበቃል›› ከጉባዔተኛው ደግሞ ‹‹የመናገር ዕድል ሊነፍገን አይገባም›› በሚል ሰዓታትን የፈጀ ጉምጉምታና ጩኸትና አዳራሹን ሞልቶት ቆየ፡፡ በየመሀሉ አንጋፋው የቅዱስ ጊዮርጊስ ስፖርት ማኅበር ይህ ሁሉ የህልውና አደጋ ተጋርጦበት እያለ፣ ችግሩን በሰከነ አግባብ ተመልክቶና ገምግሞ ለትክክለኛው ሕጋዊ ቦርድ የሚያስረክብ ‹‹መፍትሔ አፈላላጊ ኮሚቴ ማቋቋም አይሻልም ወይ? የሚሉ ድምፆች ሲሰሙ፣ ከመድረኩ ደግሞ ‹‹የክለባችን መተዳደሪያ ደንብ ይህን ይፈቅዳል ወይ? ጥያቄው ይሻሻል ከሆነ በደስታ›› በሚል ጉባዔው መቀጠሉን ሪፖርተር ታዝቧል፡፡
ጨኸቱ ረገብ ሲል ለቀረቡት ጥያቄዎች ማብራሪያ የሰጡት የቦርዱ ዋና ጸሐፊ አቶ ነዋይ ናቸው፡፡ ለዚህን ያህል ዓመታት ጠቅላላ ጉባዔ ያልተካሄደበት ምክንያት ሲያስረዱ፣ በመጀመሪያዎቹ ዓመታት በኮቪድ-19 ወረርሽኝና በሰሜኑ የኢትዮጵያ ክፍል በተነሳው ጦርነት ምክንያት፣ እንዲሁም ሁለቱ አስገዳጅ ሁነቶች መፍትሔ ካገኙ በኋላ ደግሞ፣ የስፖርት ማኅበራችን የቦርድ ሰብሳቢ በሕግ ጥላ ሥር መቆየታቸው የፈጠረው ክፍተት መሆኑን ጠቅሰው፣ ለዚህም ‹‹ጉባዔውን ይቅርታ እንጠይቃለን፤›› ብለዋል፡፡
ይህም ሆኖ በአዳራሹ የቀጠለው ጉምጉምታና ጩኸት ሊቋረጥ ባለመቻሉ፣ ጉባዔውን በታዛቢነት ሲከታተል የነበረው የኢትዮጵያ እግር ኳስ ፌዴሬሽን ዋና ሥራ አስፈጻሚ አቶ ባህሩ ጥላሁን፣ ተደጋጋሚ ማሳሰቢያዎችን ሲሰጡ ተደምጠዋል፡፡ የጉባዔው መንፈስ ከመረጋጋት ይልቅ፣ በተለይም በደጋፊዎቹ መካከል የሚስተዋለው ልዩነት እየሰፋ በመሄድ ላይ እያለ፣ የአዲስ አበባ ወጣቶችና ስፖርት ቢሮ ኃላፊ አቶ በላይ ደጀን ወደ አዳራሹ ሲገቡ ታይተዋል፡፡ በዚህ ሒደትም የቀረበው የዕቅድ ክንውንና የኦዲት ሪፖርት በጉባዔ እንዲፀድቅ ይሁንታ ማግኘት አለማግኘቱ አልተረጋገጠም ነበር፡፡
ይህ አካሄድ ባልተሟላበት አግባብ ነበር መድረኩ ቀጣዩን የቦርድ አመራሮች ምርጫ የሚያስፈጽመውን አስመራጭ ኮሚቴ ለማስመረጥ ጥረት ያደረገው፡፡ በዚህም በአዳራሹ የነበረው ጉባዔተኛ እንደገና ወደ ከፍተኛ ጩኸትና አለመግባባት ገብቶ ታይቷል፡፡
በዚህ ጊዜ ‹‹ሳልጠራና ሳልጋበዝ ጉባዔያችሁ ላይ በመገኘቴ በጣም ይቅርታ›› በማለት መናገሪያውን ከመድረኩ የተረከቡት የአዲስ አበባ ከተማ ወጣቶችና ስፖርት ቢሮ ኃላፊ አቶ በላይ ደጀን፣ ‹‹የመጣሁት ከፀጥታ ቢሮ ውዝግቦች ተነስተዋል በመባሉ ለማረጋጋትና በሰላም ጉባዔያችሁን እንድታካሂዱ ለመምከር ነው፡፡ የቅዱስ ጊዮርጊስ ደጋፊዎች በምርጫ ምክንያት ለሁለት እንዲከፈሉ አንፈልግም፣ ቅዱስ ጊዮርጊስ ምንም እንኳን በሕዝባዊ አደረጃጀት ባለቤት ያለው ክለብ ቢሆንም፣ ነገር ግን ደግሞ ሊዘነጋ የማይገባው የከተማችን ቡድን ነው፡፡ በመሆኑም እንደ ከተማ አስተዳደር ጉዳዩ ይመለከተናል፤›› በማለት ጠንከር ያለ መመርያ ሲያስተላልፉ ተደምጠዋል፡፡ በዚህም ጉባዔው ከመበተን ሊተርፍ መቻሉን ለመታዘብ ችለናል፡፡
ከአዲስ አበባ ወጣቶችና ስፖርት ቢሮ ኃላፊ የተላለፈውን መመርያ ተከትሎ ጉምጉምታውና ጩኸቱ ቀዝቀዝ ካለ በኋላ፣ መድረኩ ለጉባዔው የቀረበውን የዕቅድ ክንውንና የኦዲት ሪፖርት ማፀደቅ ሲገባው፣ በቀጥታ የሄደው የክለቡን የቦርድ አመራሮች ምርጫ የሚያስፈጽሙ ሦስት አባላት ያለውን አስመራጭ ኮሚቴ ማስመረጥ ላይ ነበር፡፡
በመጨረሻም አስመራጭ ኮሚቴው ጉባዔው በቀጣይ ክለቡን በቦርድ አመራርነት የሚያስተዳድሩ አሥር ዕጩዎችን እንዲጠቁም ካስደረገ በኋላ፣ ከአሥሩ ሰባት አባላት እንዲመረጡ አድርጓል፡፡ በዚሁ መሠረት አቶ አብነት ገብረ መስቀልና አቶ ፍሥሐ ሞላልኝ (ነዋሪነታቸው በአሜሪካ መሆኑ የተነገረላቸው)፣ አቶ ሚሊዮን ዓለሙ፣ አቶ መሐመድ ዓሊ፣ አቶ ነዋይ በየነ፣ አቶ አበባው ዘውዴና አቶ ሳምሶን አምዲሳ መመረጣቸው ይፋ ተደርጓል፡፡
a4864.en:
- Those who took part in the assembly via the internet had questions raised about them
- The club is said to have debts of more than 163 million birr

The venerable Saint George Sports Association, which is on the verge of completing a century since its founding, elected the club's board leaders at a general assembly held for the first time in six years at the Ethiopia Hotel (Global) in Bekilo Bet. When Reporter was present to attend the general assembly convened on Tikimt 16, 2018 E.C., it noticed that the hotel was under heavy guard by security forces. In the hall where the assembly was held, it also observed heavily built men standing scattered about, monitoring the assembly.

The assembly began after the sports association's supporters were admitted into the hall having been identified by ID. The one who announced that the assembly had officially begun was the board's secretary general, Ato Neway Beyene; the reason the other board leaders were absent, however, was not explained. A minute of silent prayer was held for board leaders who are no longer alive as well as for other benefactors. Next, after the sports association's plan performance for the past five years was presented, an audit report by an independent accountant was also presented.

According to the audit report presented to the assembly, the club's net assets at this time are 13,010,692 birr, and the report noted that the income the sports association ought to have received from partner organisations, particularly over the past five years, had declined greatly.

It was stated that in the process there had been delays in paying the salaries of players and employees, and in addition that the sports association currently has debts of 163,832,000 birr owed to service-providing institutions as well as in unpaid salary tax and pension. The report also noted that 22 million birr of that debt was owed to the club's president, Ato Abnet Gebremeskel. The audit report also included 41 million birr presented as uncollected from partner organisations.

Among the plan-performance report presented, it was included that the holding of the Ethiopian Premier League in only certain cities after the COVID-19 pandemic had greatly shaken the club's finances; even so, the sports association had taken over a 10,000 square metre plot in Lemi Kura Sub-city. It was also said that 2,000 square metres of that land had been taken because of corridor development, and that it is waiting to receive a new map (title deed).

It was presented in the report that the Kibur Ydnekachew Tessema Academy built in Bishoftu town is now serving as the main team's camp (residence), and that the academy was handed to private organisations to be looked after so that it would not be damaged. While the report was being presented, the club's supporters, ordinarily known by the motto "One Club, One Family," were seen split into two.

Before comments were invited on the plan performance and the audit report, Ato Abnet Gebremeskel, who had led the club's board as chairman for many years, presented a report on the sports association's current issues by means of the internet.

The Ethiopian Football Federation, which was present to follow the assembly as an observer, was given an opportunity from the podium to comment on the conduct of the assembly, particularly from the standpoint of directives and regulations, and after it raised the question, "Does the sports association's bylaw allow a report to be presented via the internet?" the assembly was allowed to continue.

Before having the plan performance and the audit report approved by vote, the podium allowed members of the assembly to comment. Following this, many hands were seen raised. Among those who got the chance to speak, not a few of the comments were as follows: "The report presented indicates that the venerable Saint George Sports Association is at present in a severe struggle for survival. Responsible for all this problem is the failure to hold the general assembly that legally should have been held every year, and for this, at this assembly, [the board] has completed its term of service. A legal body needs to be designated for this. Holding an election without the situation being investigated by an independent body is neither proper nor legal."

In particular, as the questions intensified from every direction - "How can an audit report called a five-year report be presented when it was not presented, approved and commented upon at a general assembly each year? Does the 41 million birr audit finding presented as uncollected from partner organisations mean that the agreement, when it was first made, was not based on law? And if so, why was it not possible to pursue and enforce the matter legally? The sports association's clubhouse activity was not included in the audit report; why?" - the way the podium went about trying to stop this trend became the reason for the assembly to split in two and for unnecessary wrangling to arise.

With the podium saying "Enough comments" and the assembly-goers saying "You should not deny us the chance to speak," murmuring and shouting that took hours filled the hall. In between, when voices were heard saying, "While the venerable Saint George Sports Association faces all this danger to its existence, would it not be better to establish a solution-seeking committee that would calmly examine and evaluate the problem and hand over to a properly legal board?" - Reporter observed that the assembly continued, with the podium responding, "Does our club's bylaw permit this? If the question is amended, gladly."

When the shouting subsided, it was the board's secretary general Ato Neway who gave clarification on the questions raised. Explaining the reason why a general assembly had not been held for so many years, he cited that in the first years it was because of the COVID-19 pandemic and the war that broke out in the northern part of Ethiopia, and that after those two compelling circumstances were resolved, it was because of the gap created by our sports association's board chairman remaining in legal custody; and for this he said, "We ask the assembly for forgiveness."

Even so, since the murmuring and shouting in the hall could not be stopped, Ato Bahiru Tilahun, chief executive of the Ethiopian Football Federation, who had been following the assembly as an observer, was heard giving repeated reminders. While the mood of the assembly, rather than calming down, was such that the division noticeable especially among the supporters was widening, Ato Belay Dejene, head of the Addis Ababa Youth and Sports Bureau, was seen entering the hall. In this process it had not been confirmed whether the plan performance and audit report presented had obtained the assembly's approval or not.

It was while this procedure was incomplete that the podium made the effort to have elected a nominating committee that would carry out the next election of board leaders. With this, the assembly-goers in the hall were seen entering once again into loud shouting and disagreement.

At this point, Ato Belay Dejene, head of the Addis Ababa City Youth and Sports Bureau, took the microphone from the podium, saying, "I apologise very much for being present at your assembly uncalled and uninvited," and was heard delivering a strong directive: "I came because the security bureau said that disputes had broken out, in order to calm things down and to advise you to conduct your assembly in peace. We do not want Saint George supporters to be split in two because of an election; although Saint George is a club owned by a popular organisation, it is nevertheless our city's team, which should not be forgotten. Therefore, as a city administration, the matter concerns us." Thereby we were able to observe that the assembly was saved from breaking up.

After the murmuring and shouting had cooled down following the directive delivered by the head of the Addis Ababa Youth and Sports Bureau, the podium, instead of having the plan performance and audit report presented to the assembly approved, went straight to having elected a three-member nominating committee to carry out the election of the club's board leaders.

Finally, after the nominating committee had the assembly nominate ten candidates to administer the club as board leaders going forward, it had seven members elected from among the ten. Accordingly, it was announced that Ato Abnet Gebremeskel and Ato Fisseha Molalign (who was said to be resident in America), Ato Million Alemu, Ato Mohammed Ali, Ato Neway Beyene, Ato Abebaw Zewde and Ato Samson Amdisa had been elected.

a4888.t:
Ahmed Satti, Gökhan Kavak, Mohamud Ismail Kulane
 Wednesday September 17, 2025
Somali Defense Minister Ahmed Moallim Fiqi says relations with Türkiye are at their highest level, while expressing a desire to implement major projects together.
In an interview with Anadolu, Fiqi recalled a pivotal visit to Mogadishu by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and his delegation in 2011 during a time when the al-Shabaab terrorist group had surrounded the Somali capital. “I remember that day. Indeed, just a few days later the city was liberated, and the capital has since enjoyed 14 years of independence and stability.”
Growing military and economic cooperation between Somalia and Türkiye
Fiqi pointed to the memorandum of understanding signed between the defense ministries of Somalia and Türkiye, noting the presence of advanced Turkish-made military helicopters flying overhead and armored vehicles in use by Somali forces.
“Under the framework of the memorandum of understanding, (Somali) Special Forces have also been trained by Türkiye at the TURKSOM Military Training Base," he said.
Fiqi said they aim to launch major projects and underscored the importance of strengthening economic cooperation, particularly to support the East African country’s stability.
He said Mogadishu was not secure during then-Prime Minister Erdogan’s 2011 visit, and remembered the hunger and difficult conditions faced by the Somali people at the time.
“We are truly in a better place today, and I see this relationship progressing day by day,” Fiqi said, highlighting that Türkiye’s largest embassy is located in Somalia and expressing confidence that the partnership will endure.
Since 2011, Turkish humanitarian and technical development assistance to Somalia has topped $1 billion, spanning a wide range of sectors including healthcare, education, municipal services, and infrastructure.

a4982.t:
The Fourth International Conference on Financing for Development (FfD4) has concluded in Seville, Spain, with the adoption of the Sevilla Commitment, a landmark agreement aimed at accelerating progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).
The United Nations in a statement said the conference brought together over 15,000 participants, including nearly 50 heads of state and government, to address the estimated $4 trillion annual SDG financing gap in developing countries.
It is the first inter-governmentally agreed financing for development framework since 2015, calling for system-wide changes regarding funding challenges related to the SDGs.
The Sevilla commitment and platform for action, according to the statement, outline specific measures aimed at furthering progress towards the SDGs and emphasise the role of international cooperation.
Building on previous frameworks such as the Monterrey Consensus, Doha Declaration, Addis Ababa Action Agenda, and the Pact for the Future, the Sevilla Commitment proposes system-wide changes regarding funding challenges related to the SDGs.
The conference noted several ongoing challenges, including rising debt, reduced investment, diminishing aid, and escalating trade tensions. According to data cited, approximately 3 billion people live in countries allocating more funds to interest payments than to health or education.
The statement noted that the Sevilla commitment focuses on three main areas: increasing investment for sustainable development, addressing issues related to debt and development and reforming international financial structures.
It added that the communique includes over 130 initiatives concerning implementation, capacity building, monitoring, and evaluation.
At the closing press conference, the statement said Spanish Economy Minister Carlos Cuerpo stated that the outcomes aim to support multilateral cooperation and efforts to advance sustainable development globally.
In her closing remarks, the United Nations Deputy Secretary-General Amina Mohammed said “the human consequences of rising debt burdens, escalating trade tensions and steep cuts to official development assistance have been brought into sharp relief this week.
“Yet, against this sobering backdrop, the Sevilla conference delivered a strong response a unifying outcome document focused on solutions that reaffirms the Addis Ababa commitments made a decade ago, renews hope through the SDGs, and shows that multilateral cooperation still matters and still works. Let FFD4 be remembered as a conference where the world chose cooperation over fragmentation, unity over division and action over inertia.”

a4994.t:
Sep 2 , 2023
Ethiopia has housed nearly 300,000 Sudanese refugees who fled the breakout of a five-month-long widespread conflict. The hospitality was commended by the United Nations' designated expert on Human Rights in Sudan, Radhouane Nouice as he briefed the devastating conditions in the embattled country at the Economic Commission of Africa (ECA) headquarters last week. With 20 million in need of assistance, 4.5 million displaced from their homes and the destruction of the health infrastructure in the country, Radhoune indicated efforts for humanitarian assistance are hampered by a shortage of funding, inability to obtain visas and blockage of access. Radhoune called for the cessation of "the senseless conflict" as he outlined the horrendous living conditions where summary executions, widespread assault and violence were cited as tragic developments. "There are no winners, with only the people losing," he said.

a4997.t:
Independent Flowers for ArcelorMittal Liberia -Roaming Journalists Peep Inside Railway Upgrade, Expansion
One of the elements of news – credibility or believability – as communication experts would put it, comes about more often than not when the reportage comes from external and independent reporters rather from internal and compromised sources. This is perhaps exactly what those who are following the operations of one of Liberia’s premier foreign concessionaires, ArcelorMittal Liberia, will get as two critical journalists carried out a sudden investigative tour of the company’s facilities, mainly its railway. At the end of the tour, radio journalists Austin Kawah and Kelvin Demey produced a report titled, “A Railway Reborn: An exclusive look inside ArcelorMittal Liberia’s bold upgrade and expansion of Liberia’s railway.” The Analyst obtained a syndicated copy, as published unedited on page 2 of this edition.
By: Austin Kawah and Kelvin Demey
Buchanan, October 3, 2024
At approximately 11 a.m. on September 24, 2024, we boarded the ArcelorMittal Liberia (AML) helicopter for an aerial view of their rail operations, followed by an on-the-ground tour and an interview with Edwin Tokpa, Rail Operations Manager and one of Liberia’s own, leading the transformation. We will share more from our interview with Tokpa in subsequent articles. Our recent tour marks the first time the media is granted exclusive access to AML’s efforts in our country, and we are here to provide a first-hand account of what we witnessed.
As AMLs helicopter rose over the newly built tracks glistening in the morning light, the scope of ArcelorMittal Liberia’s transformation of the Buchanan railway station was impossible to miss. Below us, a network of shiny steel rails stretched out like veins, connecting the vital infrastructure that’s powering Liberia’s economic ambitions. The scene buzzed with activity as bulldozers and cranes worked alongside skilled crews installing state-of-the-art equipment—everything from a rail car dumper to an intricate conveyor system. It was clear: ArcelorMittal Liberia is serious about shaping the future of mining and exports in Liberia.
Our day began with a downpour, drenching the site and giving us an unfiltered look at the intensity of operations. We know it is raining season in our country now, but experiencing this in a mining environment, demonstrates the dedication of our Liberians working hard to reinvigorate Liberia’s economy, with AML providing extensive support. Yet, despite the rain, the mood was one of determination, a feeling only amplified by seeing Liberians leading these efforts.
The sheer scale of the construction and upgrades was staggering, reflecting ArcelorMittal’s bold expansion project, not just for Liberia, but for Africa and the global iron ore market. Currently Liberia is being placed on the mining map, as a key forerunner to the second largest mining investment project on our African continent. We hope that from this, other investors will come to our country with the same dedication and determination that AML has shown.
The Yekepa-Buchanan railway, we learned, is central to this plan. As the company races toward completing a concentrator in Tokadeh, Nimba County, production is set to triple from 5 million tonnes of iron ore annually to 15 million, with a goal to reach 30 million tonnes per year. This is a significant investment for our country, one that stands to be truly transformational for the lives of many Liberians.
This rail line, once reduced to ruin during Liberia’s civil war, has been painstakingly rebuilt by ArcelorMittal Liberia. Now, it stands as an asset owned by the Liberian government and maintained by ArcelorMittal, critical to the country’s economic growth. The upgrades are ambitious, restoring full capacity while enhancing safety and security, which we saw first-hand during our visit.
However, not everyone seems to appreciate the extent of these efforts. ArcelorMittal has faced its share of challenges, with attempts to undermine the company’s investment through misinformation. These narratives have distracted from the tangible benefits the railway brings—job creation, revenue, and infrastructure development—and instead, offered empty promises from entities with little to no real investment in Liberia.
To truly understand the depth of ArcelorMittal’s investment, we took an exclusive flyover of the Yekepa-Buchanan railway. From above, it became clear how vital this infrastructure is to Liberia’s mining sector. Stretching across the landscape, the rail was in various stages of refurbishment, with notable improvements already in place. A particularly impressive feature was the transition from aging timber sleepers to durable steel ones, a move that will significantly boost the railway’s longevity and safety. The engineers we spoke with explained that these steel sleepers have a life expectancy of about 50 years—an investment in the future.
ArcelorMittal has also gone the extra mile with anti-theft measures, implementing high-end solutions like anti-theft fasteners, a response to the persistent issue of rail material theft. This commitment to safeguarding their operations reflects a broader strategy of long-term investment in Liberia.
Perhaps one of the most exciting developments we observed was the construction of a rail car dumper in Buchanan, part of the company’s Phase II expansion. This automatic offloading station is set to revolutionize the iron ore transportation process, streamlining operations, and boosting the port’s export capacity. We saw firsthand how this facility will reduce manual handling, increasing efficiency and setting the stage for future growth.
The upgrades don’t stop there. ArcelorMittal is bringing in 500 new wagons and nine new locomotives, further increasing operational efficiency. What’s more, the company is creating additional capacity on the railway to accommodate other users—an initiative that underscores their commitment to shared infrastructure that benefits Liberia.
Throughout the tour, we saw the pride that Liberians have in these efforts, from the engineers on the ground to the officials overseeing the massive upgrades. ArcelorMittal’s focus on building local capacity was evident in every corner of the operation. Liberians are not just benefiting from this investment—they are driving it.
Liberians constitute over 98-percent of the about seven hundred-member workforce of ArcelorMittal Rail and Port Departments.
For all the progress, however, the company faces significant hurdles in maintaining the railway, particularly due to theft. To combat this, ArcelorMittal has ramped up security, installing a new Positive Train Control System and strengthening community collaborations to protect the railway. Company officials stressed that this rail line belongs to the people of Liberia, and it’s up to all of us—local communities, government, and companies alike—to protect this critical asset.
As our visit came to an end, what struck me most was not just the scale of ArcelorMittal’s investment, but the clear sense that this railway is more than just a line of steel connecting towns and mines—it’s a lifeline for Liberia’s economic future. The Yekepa-Buchanan railway has risen from the ashes of war thanks to ArcelorMittal’s commitment and is poised to play a key role in positioning Liberia as a serious player in the global iron ore market.
This railway is not just about ArcelorMittal’s operations. It’s about Liberia’s future. AML, we hope to come and see you again, it is always welcoming when foreign entities in our country are truly being serious and investing in our country.

a5160.t:
Un responsable de la surveillance de l'agence américaine d'aide internationale USAID a été limogé par le gouvernement peu après la publication d'un rapport sur les conséquences de son démantèlement, ont affirmé mercredi plusieurs médias américains.
Paul Martin, inspecteur général pour l'USAID, a reçu mardi un courriel d'un membre de la Maison Blanche, l'informant "qu'au nom du Président Donald Trump (...) votre rôle d'inspecteur général de l'Agence des États-Unis pour le développement international est résilié, avec effet immédiat", selon le Washington Post.
Cette décision lui a été notifiée au lendemain de la publication par ses services d'un rapport sur les effets du démantèlement de l'USAID décidé par Donald Trump, et alors que le président américain a limogé plus d'une dizaine d'inspecteurs généraux de différents organismes depuis sa prise de fonction fin janvier.
L'administration américaine entend licencier près de 90% des quelque 10.000 employés de l'agence, mais la justice a pour l'instant suspendu le plan de départ.
Le démantèlement de l'USAID aurait de conséquences massives pour de nombreuses ONG dans le monde qui dépendent de l'aide et des financements américains, et aurait un lourd impact sur l'influence américaine dans le monde, l'USAID étant un outil majeur de "soft power".
Cette agence gère un budget de 42,8 milliards de dollars, qui à lui seul représente 42% de l'aide humanitaire déboursée dans le monde.
Donald Trump entend mettre un terme aux "problèmes de fraude, de gaspillage, d'abus" des multiples organes gouvernementaux américains, et accuse l'USAID de malversations, affirmant que "la corruption" y est "à des niveaux jamais vus", a-t-il assuré, sans étayer son propos.
Le rapport publié lundi se penche sur les "risques et défis pour la sauvegarde et la distribution des 8,2 milliards de dollars de l'USAID en fonds d'aide humanitaire engagés mais non décaissés" du fait de la suspension des programmes d'aide étrangère décidée par le Département d'Etat et la décision de réduire les effectifs de l'agence, "qui ont considérablement réduit la capacité opérationnelle de son Bureau d'assistance humanitaire (BHA)".
La réduction des effectifs limitera la capacité du BHA de l'USAID "à empêcher que de l'aide humanitaire soit bloquée pour d'éventuels liens avec des groupes terroristes, et à surveiller les livraisons d'aide dans des environnements à haut risque", estime-t-il.
La suspension de l'aide rend elle incertaine la situation de "plus de 489 millions de dollars d'aide alimentaire dans les ports, en transit et dans les entrepôts", qui risquent de se détériorer, nécessitent de trouver des lieux de stockage, et risquent d'être détournés.
a5160.en:
A USAID oversight official has been fired after a critical report on the dismantling

An official responsible for oversight of the US international aid agency USAID was fired by the government shortly after the publication of a report on the consequences of its dismantling, several American media outlets reported on Wednesday.

Paul Martin, inspector general for USAID, received an email on Tuesday from a member of the White House informing him “that on behalf of President Donald Trump (...) your role as inspector general of the United States Agency for International Development is terminated, effective immediately,” according to the Washington Post.

The decision was notified to him the day after his office published a report on the effects of the dismantling of USAID decided by Donald Trump, and at a time when the American president has fired more than a dozen inspectors general of various bodies since taking office in late January.

The US administration intends to lay off nearly 90% of the agency’s some 10,000 employees, but the courts have for now suspended the departure plan.

The dismantling of USAID would have massive consequences for many NGOs around the world that depend on American aid and funding, and would have a heavy impact on American influence in the world, USAID being a major instrument of “soft power.”

The agency manages a budget of $42.8 billion, which alone represents 42% of humanitarian aid disbursed worldwide.

Donald Trump intends to put an end to the “problems of fraud, waste, abuse” of the many American government bodies, and accuses USAID of misconduct, asserting that “corruption” there is “at levels never seen before,” he claimed, without substantiating his statement.

The report published on Monday examines the “risks and challenges for safeguarding and distributing USAID’s $8.2 billion in humanitarian aid funds that are committed but not disbursed” as a result of the suspension of foreign aid programs decided by the State Department and the decision to cut the agency’s staff, “which have considerably reduced the operational capacity of its Bureau for Humanitarian Assistance (BHA).”

The staff reduction will limit the capacity of USAID’s BHA “to prevent humanitarian aid from being diverted because of possible links with terrorist groups, and to monitor aid deliveries in high-risk environments,” it estimates.

The aid suspension makes uncertain the situation of “more than $489 million of food aid in ports, in transit and in warehouses,” which risks deteriorating, requires finding storage locations, and risks being diverted.

a5166.t:
MONROVIA, LIBERIA-The Liberian Government has filed a lawsuit against the Management of Green Park over accountability issues.
The Green Park Management is running the affairs of parks built by the immediate passed Government of Liberia.
The parks include the PHP, Invincible Sports, New Kru Town, Doe Community and the West Point Parks.
According to Information Minister Jerolinmek Piah, the move by the Government is based on an audit report from the General Auditing Commission (GAC).
Minister Piah revealed that the GAC’S report shows that the Management of the Green Park has only been collecting money from Liberians with no accountability and impact in return.
Information Minister Jerolinmek Piah said:” The Management of the Green Park entered a twenty-year verbal agreement with past authorities of the MCC, and that the Management has no records of competence to handle such business.”
By: Augustine Saah

a5461.t:
“The integrity of the upright guides them, but the unfaithful are destroyed by their duplicity.” – Proverbs 11:3 (NIV)
INTRODUCTION
In every generation, leadership stands or falls on three key pillars: calling, competence, and character. While calling brings purpose and competence ensures effectiveness, it is character that sustains and validates leadership over time. Without godly character, even the most gifted leaders risk failure.
One biblical figure who beautifully exemplifies the integration of these three pillars is Nehemiah. He was a man with a divine calling, exceptional administrative skill, and an incorruptible character rooted in his relationship with God. At a time of national crisis and moral decay, Nehemiah rose to the challenge, not only rebuilding Jerusalem’s broken walls but also restoring the people’s covenant commitment to God.
Today, we reflect on the rich character traits Nehemiah displayed in leadership — traits that are urgently needed in our time. As we examine his life, we are also called to emulate him, ultimately pointing our lives to the perfect model of leadership and character — Jesus Christ.
v A MAN OF CALLING AND COURAGE
Nehemiah’s leadership journey begins not on a public platform but in the quiet place of prayer. When his brother Hanani brought word of Jerusalem’s disgrace, Nehemiah was deeply moved — not merely with emotion, but with a sense of divine urgency. His response was immediate: he mourned, fasted, and prayed.
This is where character begins — not in the limelight but in the heart that is attuned to God’s burden. Nehemiah recognized that the brokenness of his people was spiritual before it was structural. He confessed sin — his own and that of his people — acknowledging their collective failure before God. This humility and honesty marked his entire leadership journey.
When the time came to act, Nehemiah did not hesitate. He boldly asked King Artaxerxes for permission, letters of authority, and material provisions for the work. His courage was matched by strategic thinking — proving that faith and planning are not opposites, but companions.
v COMPETENCE ROOTED IN PRAYER AND WISDOM
Once in Jerusalem, Nehemiah’s leadership moved into action. He did not start with noise or fanfare. He first inspected the damage quietly, assessing the scope of work. This showed foresight and discernment — a leader who takes time to understand before rushing to fix.
Nehemiah’s competence as a builder and organizer is unmistakable. He assigned work based on skill, geography, and family units. He delegated effectively, honored contributions, and built unity among a diverse group of people. His leadership was inclusive, empowering, and responsive to the strengths of others.
Yet his real strength lay not just in administration, but in spiritual sensitivity. He constantly sought God’s direction — from facing enemies like Sanballat and Tobiah to dealing with internal complaints and economic injustice. At every turn, Nehemiah prayed, acted wisely, and stayed grounded in his mission.
v CONFRONTING EVIL WITH MORAL COURAGE
One of Nehemiah’s most admirable traits was his refusal to compromise with sin. After twelve years of faithful service, he left Jerusalem briefly and returned to find the people had fallen again into disobedience. The Levites had abandoned their temple duties due to unpaid tithes, the Sabbath was being profaned through business, and intermarriage with foreigners had resumed.
Nehemiah did not ignore these issues. He confronted them with moral clarity and boldness — actions that many leaders today might find uncomfortable. He cleansed the temple, reinstated the Levites, commanded Sabbath observance, and rebuked those who had married foreign women in violation of God’s law.
What gave Nehemiah this moral authority? It was the consistency of his character. His private devotion matched his public leadership. Like Phinehas in Numbers 25, whose zeal for God’s holiness brought divine approval, Nehemiah’s intolerance for compromise won God’s favor and restored spiritual order.
In every act, Nehemiah proved that leadership is not about pleasing people, but about honoring God — even when it means taking unpopular stands. This kind of leadership transforms nations, churches, and homes.
v POINTING US TO CHRIST
Ultimately, Nehemiah’s life and leadership foreshadow the perfect character of our Lord Jesus Christ. Like Nehemiah, Jesus wept over Jerusalem, called people to repentance, and acted boldly against corruption in the temple. He, too, rebuilt what was broken — not with bricks and mortar, but with grace and truth, laying the foundation for a new covenant.
Every leader is called to walk as Jesus walked (1 John 2:6), and Nehemiah gives us a tangible example of how to do so in a broken world. He teaches us to be sensitive to God’s voice, courageous in opposition, wise in administration, and unwavering in moral truth.
CONCLUSION
Nehemiah’s legacy reminds us that godly character is not an optional trait in leadership — it is the very heart of it. In a world that often rewards charisma over character and ambition over integrity, Nehemiah stands as a timeless model of a leader after God’s own heart.
Let every pastor, parent, teacher, youth leader, executive, and public servant take to heart the example Nehemiah set. His story is not merely historical; it is profoundly relevant. It teaches us that godly leadership begins with prayer, is sustained by wisdom, and is proven in moral courage.
Most of all, his life points us to the One who is the true and better Nehemiah — Jesus Christ — who calls each of us to lead with humility, serve with faithfulness, and build what is broken with His strength and truth.
Remain Blessed!

a5521.t:
L’ambassade du Canada au Burkina Faso a célébré en avance la fête nationale canadienne le jeudi 26 juin 2025, à Ouagadougou. Cette célébration a été l’occasion de mettre en lumière les liens historiques et durables qui unissent les deux pays.
Normalement commémorée chaque 1er juillet, la fête nationale canadienne a été célébrée le 26 juin 2025 par l’ambassade du Canada au Burkina Faso. Dès l’ouverture des festivités, Tina Guthrie, l’ambassadrice du Canada au Burkina Faso, a salué les plus de 60 ans d’amitié et de coopération qui lient le Burkina Faso et le Canada.
L’ambassadrice Guthrie a souligné que cette coopération se traduit par des actions concrètes dans les domaines humanitaire, économique et de la santé. « Près de 17 millions de repas scolaires ont été servis, y compris dans des zones confrontées à de forts défis sécuritaires, tout en soutenant 9 000 producteurs locaux pour l’approvisionnement des cantines scolaires.
Notre aide humanitaire a touché 1,6 million de personnes déplacées ou vulnérables. Dans le nord du Burkina Faso, le Canada contribue également à renforcer l’accès aux soins de santé dans les zones touchées par les conflits », a-t-elle énuméré.
Sur le plan économique, l’ambassadrice a noté que les entreprises canadiennes présentes au Burkina Faso créent de l’emploi, de la richesse et de l’innovation, tout en respectant les normes nationales et les standards internationaux les plus élevés.
« Les compagnies minières canadiennes continuent de jouer un rôle de premier plan dans le développement du secteur minier burkinabè. Elles ont maintenu leurs opérations, et une usine minière est même en expansion, preuve d’un engagement à long terme au Burkina Faso », a-t-elle ajouté.
Lire aussi : La fête nationale du Canada célébrée au Burkina Faso
De son côté, Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, le ministre des Affaires étrangères du Burkina Faso, a exprimé la reconnaissance du gouvernement burkinabè envers le peuple canadien. Il a également salué les efforts du Canada dans le développement du secteur privé burkinabè.
« Le Burkina et le Canada, c’est plus de 60 années de marche et de coopération, où nous avons appris à nous connaître, à identifier ensemble des projets, à les réaliser et à poser de nouvelles actions dans plusieurs domaines. Aujourd’hui, nous avons suffisamment de recul pour apprécier cette coopération qui a permis d’avoir des résultats concrets sur le terrain dans divers secteurs.
Nous essayons de situer nos partenaires dans un esprit d’équilibre gagnant-gagnant. Aujourd’hui, le Canada, qui a beaucoup investi dans le secteur minier, a permis au Burkina Faso d’avoir une certaine coordination, de prendre conscience de ses potentialités et d’améliorer sa politique en matière de gestion minière », a déclaré.
Aurelle KIENDREBEOGO (stagiaire)
Aminata Catherine SANOU
Burkina 24
a5521.en:
The Embassy of Canada in Burkina Faso celebrated the Canadian national holiday early, on Thursday 26 June 2025, in Ouagadougou. The celebration was an opportunity to highlight the historic and lasting ties that unite the two countries.

Normally commemorated each 1 July, the Canadian national holiday was celebrated on 26 June 2025 by the Embassy of Canada in Burkina Faso. From the opening of the festivities, Tina Guthrie, Canada’s Ambassador to Burkina Faso, hailed the more than 60 years of friendship and cooperation that bind Burkina Faso and Canada.

Ambassador Guthrie stressed that this cooperation translates into concrete actions in the humanitarian, economic and health fields. “Nearly 17 million school meals have been served, including in areas facing major security challenges, while supporting 9,000 local producers for the supply of school canteens. Our humanitarian aid has reached 1.6 million displaced or vulnerable people. In northern Burkina Faso, Canada is also helping to strengthen access to health care in conflict-affected areas,” she listed.

On the economic front, the ambassador noted that Canadian companies present in Burkina Faso create employment, wealth and innovation, while respecting national norms and the highest international standards.

“Canadian mining companies continue to play a leading role in the development of Burkina Faso’s mining sector. They have maintained their operations, and one mining plant is even expanding, proof of a long-term commitment to Burkina Faso,” she added.

Read also: Canada’s national holiday celebrated in Burkina Faso

For his part, Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, Burkina Faso’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, expressed the Burkinabè government’s gratitude to the Canadian people. He also hailed Canada’s efforts in the development of the Burkinabè private sector.

“Burkina and Canada is more than 60 years of walking together and of cooperation, in which we have learned to know one another, to identify projects together, to carry them out and to undertake new actions in several fields. Today we have enough hindsight to appreciate this cooperation, which has made it possible to obtain concrete results on the ground in various sectors. We try to situate our partners in a spirit of win-win balance. Today, Canada, which has invested a great deal in the mining sector, has enabled Burkina Faso to have a certain coordination, to become aware of its potential and to improve its mining management policy,” he declared.

Aurelle KIENDREBEOGO (intern)
Aminata Catherine SANOU
Burkina 24

a5576.t:
Ceci est une tribune indépendante de Mamadou Sissoko, analyste politique, sur l’actualité internationale.
L’Algérie fait face à une situation géopolitique complexe, à la croisée de menaces internes et externes qui mettent à l’épreuve sa souveraineté et la stabilité de ses frontières. Le Front de libération de l’Azawad (FLA), dirigé par Alghabass Ag Intalla, progresse dans le nord du Mali, à proximité immédiate des frontières algériennes, et exprime des ambitions clairement affichées de créer un État touareg unifié.
Dans ses déclarations, Ag Intalla a souligné que « les frontières de l’Afrique sont artificielles, tracées à la règle par les colonisateurs, sans respect pour nos peuples ni pour nos terres », affirmant que ces limites ont déchiré les familles, les tribus et interrompu des routes nomades qui reliaient les hommes depuis des siècles.
Il insiste sur le fait que le peuple touareg, dispersé entre le Mali, le Niger, l’Algérie, la Libye et le Burkina Faso, est uni par son sang, sa culture et son histoire, et qu’il ne s’agit ni d’une minorité ni d’une tribu, mais d’un peuple unique du Sahara qui doit retrouver son unité historique.
Ces déclarations, combinées à la progression militaire du FLA près des frontières algériennes, montrent que le mouvement pourrait empiéter sur le sud algérien, notamment dans les régions de Tamanrasset et d’Adrar, riches en or et en uranium, ce qui accroît le risque stratégique pour l’Algérie.
Le contexte international amplifie encore la complexité de la situation. Le New Lines Institute, un think tank américain influent, a récemment publié un rapport recommandé par certains experts, qui propose une intervention américaine immédiate dans le sud algérien, mais précise que cette intervention ne devrait pas être militaire.
Le rapport suggère de soutenir des recherches locales via des institutions algériennes, de privilégier des mécanismes d’aide ciblés et de mobiliser les organisations de la diaspora touareg comme intermédiaires civiques. Bien que présenté comme une approche visant à promouvoir la démocratie et les droits humains, ce type d’intervention pourrait en réalité légitimer des revendications séparatistes et créer un levier politique et économique pour exercer une influence indirecte sur le sud algérien.
Dans ce cadre, le FLA pourrait devenir un instrument militaire et politique au service de cette stratégie américaine, capable de soutenir des pressions contre l’État algérien et d’assurer un accès indirect aux ressources stratégiques.
Des observateurs pensent que le projet d’une “Grande Azawad” pourrait également bénéficier d’un soutien implicite de l’Europe, et particulièrement de la France, alliée stratégique des États-Unis au sein du NATO.
Ce projet sécessionniste sert directement les intérêts français, qui cherchent à retrouver l’influence qu’ils ont perdue en Afrique, notamment dans le Sahel et en Algérie. Selon eux, un État touareg aligné sur les intérêts occidentaux offrirait à la France un levier politique et économique considérable, tout en affaiblissant la souveraineté algérienne. Les déclarations du FLA et l’expansion de ses positions militaires représentent donc un instrument idéal pour justifier et faciliter cette stratégie, en donnant un prétexte diplomatique et médiatique à l’implication occidentale.
Parallèlement, des actions non militaires sont prévues pour préparer le terrain à cette influence. Les experts indiquent que les organisations humanitaires seront mobilisées dans le sud algérien pour documenter la situation et signaler les violations supposées des droits humains, tout en donnant une légitimité internationale à une intervention diplomatique indirecte.
De plus, les organisations touarègues opposées au gouvernement algérien, à l’intérieur comme à l’extérieur du pays, pourraient bénéficier de soutien et de protection, afin d’affaiblir la cohésion nationale et de légitimer les revendications séparatistes.
Ces mesures combinées à la montée en puissance du FLA montrent que Washington et ses alliés peuvent transformer le mouvement en un outil stratégique pour atteindre des objectifs géopolitiques et économiques, tout en limitant les risques d’une confrontation militaire directe.
Face à cette double menace, les mêmes experts estiment que l’Algérie doit adopter une stratégie proactive et complète. Le renforcement de la sécurité dans le sud, à travers des mesures militaires adaptées au terrain et des initiatives civiles visant à stabiliser les populations locales, est indispensable. Ils ajoutent que l’État doit également jouer un rôle de médiateur entre le FLA et le gouvernement malien, comme lors des négociations de 2015, afin de prévenir toute propagation de l’instabilité malienne sur son territoire.
La prise en compte des préoccupations légitimes des communautés touarègues locales, par l’inclusion économique, sociale et politique, est essentielle pour réduire la tentation d’alignement sur des acteurs externes. Parallèlement, la vigilance face aux initiatives étrangères, en particulier celles des États-Unis et de la France, est primordiale pour contrecarrer toute tentative d’ingérence déguisée en aide humanitaire ou diplomatique et pour protéger la souveraineté nationale ainsi que les ressources stratégiques du sud.
En conclusion, l’expansion du FLA et les ambitions d’Alghabass Ag Intalla, combinées à l’intérêt stratégique des puissances occidentales, représentent une menace majeure pour l’intégrité territoriale et la stabilité de l’Algérie. La convergence entre les objectifs séparatistes locaux et l’agenda international, avec le soutien potentiel des organisations humanitaires et des réseaux de la diaspora, crée un risque réel de fragmentation et de déstabilisation.
La vigilance, la médiation proactive et l’inclusion des communautés locales restent les clés pour protéger la souveraineté nationale, sécuriser les ressources stratégiques et prévenir toute escalade susceptible de fragiliser la paix et l’unité nationale.
Mamadou Sissoko
Analyste politique indépendant
a5576.en:
This is an independent opinion piece by Mamadou Sissoko, political analyst, on international current affairs.

Algeria faces a complex geopolitical situation, at the crossroads of internal and external threats that test its sovereignty and the stability of its borders. The Azawad Liberation Front (FLA), led by Alghabass Ag Intalla, is advancing in northern Mali, in the immediate vicinity of the Algerian borders, and expresses clearly stated ambitions to create a unified Tuareg state.

In his statements, Ag Intalla stressed that "Africa's borders are artificial, drawn with a ruler by the colonisers, without respect for our peoples or our lands", asserting that these boundaries have torn apart families and tribes and cut off nomadic routes that had linked people for centuries.

He insists that the Tuareg people, dispersed among Mali, Niger, Algeria, Libya and Burkina Faso, are united by their blood, their culture and their history, and that they are neither a minority nor a tribe, but a single people of the Sahara who must recover their historical unity.

These statements, combined with the FLA's military advance near the Algerian borders, show that the movement could encroach on southern Algeria, notably in the regions of Tamanrasset and Adrar, rich in gold and uranium, which increases the strategic risk for Algeria.

The international context further amplifies the complexity of the situation. The New Lines Institute, an influential American think tank, recently published a report recommended by certain experts, which proposes an immediate American intervention in southern Algeria, but specifies that this intervention should not be military.

The report suggests supporting local research through Algerian institutions, favouring targeted aid mechanisms and mobilising Tuareg diaspora organisations as civic intermediaries. Although presented as an approach aimed at promoting democracy and human rights, this type of intervention could in reality legitimise separatist claims and create political and economic leverage to exert indirect influence over southern Algeria.

In this framework, the FLA could become a military and political instrument in the service of this American strategy, capable of supporting pressure against the Algerian state and ensuring indirect access to strategic resources.

Observers believe that the "Greater Azawad" project could also benefit from implicit support from Europe, and particularly from France, a strategic ally of the United States within NATO.

This secessionist project directly serves French interests, which seek to recover the influence France has lost in Africa, notably in the Sahel and in Algeria. According to them, a Tuareg state aligned with Western interests would offer France considerable political and economic leverage, while weakening Algerian sovereignty. The FLA's statements and the expansion of its military positions therefore represent an ideal instrument to justify and facilitate this strategy, by providing a diplomatic and media pretext for Western involvement.

At the same time, non-military actions are planned to prepare the ground for this influence. Experts indicate that humanitarian organisations will be mobilised in southern Algeria to document the situation and report alleged human rights violations, while giving international legitimacy to an indirect diplomatic intervention.

In addition, Tuareg organisations opposed to the Algerian government, both inside and outside the country, could benefit from support and protection, in order to weaken national cohesion and legitimise separatist claims.

These measures, combined with the rise of the FLA, show that Washington and its allies can transform the movement into a strategic tool to achieve geopolitical and economic objectives, while limiting the risks of a direct military confrontation.

Faced with this dual threat, the same experts consider that Algeria must adopt a proactive and comprehensive strategy. Strengthening security in the south, through military measures adapted to the terrain and civil initiatives aimed at stabilising local populations, is indispensable. They add that the state must also play a mediating role between the FLA and the Malian government, as it did during the 2015 negotiations, in order to prevent any spread of Malian instability onto its territory.

Taking into account the legitimate concerns of local Tuareg communities, through economic, social and political inclusion, is essential to reduce the temptation to align with external actors. At the same time, vigilance regarding foreign initiatives, particularly those of the United States and France, is paramount in order to counter any attempt at interference disguised as humanitarian or diplomatic aid and to protect national sovereignty as well as the strategic resources of the south.

In conclusion, the expansion of the FLA and the ambitions of Alghabass Ag Intalla, combined with the strategic interest of the Western powers, represent a major threat to the territorial integrity and stability of Algeria. The convergence between local separatist objectives and the international agenda, with the potential support of humanitarian organisations and diaspora networks, creates a real risk of fragmentation and destabilisation.

Vigilance, proactive mediation and the inclusion of local communities remain the keys to protecting national sovereignty, securing strategic resources and preventing any escalation likely to weaken peace and national unity.

Mamadou Sissoko
Independent political analyst

a5608.t:
Dans un contexte d’urgence humanitaire extrême à Gaza, où les hôpitaux sont à bout de souffle et où des bébés meurent de malnutrition faute de lait et de soins, le Maroc a annoncé l’envoi d’une aide humanitaire et médicale d’envergure.
Le communiqué du ministère des Affaires étrangères marocain indique que Sa Majesté le Roi Mohammed VI, Président du Comité Al-Qods, a ordonné l’acheminement immédiat à Gaza de près de 180 tonnes de denrées alimentaires, de lait pour enfants, de médicaments, de matériel chirurgical et d’abris d’urgence. Cette cargaison vitale, comprenant également des tentes et couvertures, sera transportée par un couloir spécialement aménagé pour garantir sa livraison directe aux populations palestiniennes.
Une réponse à une crise humanitaire d’une ampleur inédite
Depuis plusieurs semaines, la bande de Gaza est confrontée à un blocus total qui a plongé la population dans la famine. Les agences humanitaires alertent sur des cas de décès de nourrissons, faute de lait infantile, et sur l’effondrement des services de santé. Les hôpitaux, privés d’électricité et de matériel, ne parviennent plus à sauver les plus vulnérables.
Dans ce contexte dramatique, le geste marocain revêt une portée symbolique et opérationnelle majeure. Il témoigne d’une solidarité active, bien au-delà des déclarations de principe. En intégrant dans son aide des produits spécifiquement destinés aux enfants, Rabat répond directement à l’une des urgences les plus criantes de cette crise : sauver des vies infantiles menacées par la faim et les maladies évitables.
Un engagement constant du Maroc envers la cause palestinienne
Ce nouvel envoi s’inscrit dans la continuité des actions entreprises par le Royaume pour soutenir la population palestinienne. Sous l’impulsion du Souverain, le Maroc a multiplié ces dernières années les initiatives humanitaires et politiques en faveur de Gaza, tout en plaidant pour une solution juste et durable au conflit.
En prenant cette décision dans un moment où la communauté internationale peine à mobiliser des corridors humanitaires efficaces, le Maroc renforce son rôle de partenaire fiable et engagé pour les Palestiniens.
Un signal à la communauté internationale
Au-delà de l’aide matérielle, ce geste interpelle les acteurs internationaux sur leur responsabilité face à une catastrophe humanitaire qui prend des proportions alarmantes. La famine qui frappe les enfants de Gaza ne résulte pas seulement de pénuries logistiques, mais d’un contexte politique où l’accès à l’aide est souvent entravé.
Le Maroc, par cet acte concret, rappelle que la solidarité ne peut attendre quand des vies innocentes, notamment celles des bébés, sont en jeu.
MK/ac/Sf/APA
a5608.en:
Morocco-Gaza: vital aid in the face of famine (analysis)

Amid an extreme humanitarian emergency in Gaza, where hospitals are at breaking point and babies are dying of malnutrition for lack of milk and care, Morocco has announced the dispatch of large-scale humanitarian and medical aid.

The communiqué of the Moroccan Ministry of Foreign Affairs states that His Majesty King Mohammed VI, President of the Al-Quds Committee, has ordered the immediate delivery to Gaza of nearly 180 tonnes of foodstuffs, children's milk, medicines, surgical equipment and emergency shelters. This vital cargo, which also includes tents and blankets, will be transported through a specially arranged corridor to guarantee its direct delivery to the Palestinian population.

A response to a humanitarian crisis of unprecedented scale

For several weeks, the Gaza Strip has faced a total blockade that has plunged the population into famine. Humanitarian agencies are warning of cases of infant deaths for lack of baby milk, and of the collapse of health services. Hospitals, deprived of electricity and equipment, can no longer save the most vulnerable.

In this dramatic context, the Moroccan gesture carries major symbolic and operational significance. It demonstrates active solidarity, going well beyond declarations of principle. By including in its aid products specifically intended for children, Rabat responds directly to one of the most glaring emergencies of this crisis: saving young lives threatened by hunger and preventable diseases.

Morocco's steadfast commitment to the Palestinian cause

This new shipment continues the actions undertaken by the Kingdom to support the Palestinian population. Under the Sovereign's impetus, Morocco has in recent years multiplied humanitarian and political initiatives in favour of Gaza, while advocating for a just and lasting solution to the conflict.

By taking this decision at a moment when the international community is struggling to mobilise effective humanitarian corridors, Morocco strengthens its role as a reliable and committed partner for the Palestinians.

A signal to the international community

Beyond material aid, this gesture challenges international actors on their responsibility in the face of a humanitarian catastrophe that is taking on alarming proportions. The famine striking the children of Gaza results not only from logistical shortages, but from a political context in which access to aid is often obstructed.

Morocco, through this concrete act, reminds us that solidarity cannot wait when innocent lives, particularly those of babies, are at stake.

MK/ac/Sf/APA

a5769.t:
The Medicines Control Agency (MCA) has issued an urgent warning to the public, declaring it illegal to import, distribute, store, or sell medical devices, including in vitro diagnostics, without proper authorization in The Gambia. The announcement, made under the Medicines and Related Products Act of 2014, underscores the agency’s mandate to ensure the quality, safety, and efficacy of medicines and related products, including medical devices, herbal medicines, cosmetics, and household chemicals.
The MCA highlighted global concerns over substandard and falsified medical devices, particularly in vitro diagnostics, which can produce inaccurate laboratory results, leading to misdiagnoses, improper treatment, and increased health risks, such as higher morbidity and mortality. Citing recommendations from the World Health Organization and the African Union, the agency emphasized the need for stringent regulation to protect public safety.
All individuals and entities engaged in the trade of medical devices are required to obtain authorization from the MCA. Noncompliance with the Medicines and Related Substances Act, 1965, and the Medicines and Related Substances Regulations, 2011, will result in severe regulatory sanctions.
The public is encouraged to contact the MCA for further information via their toll-free QCell line at 1233, by calling 3363068, or by visiting their offices.

a5779.t:
Abdoulaye Diop: l'Ukraine menace la sécurité en Afrique
Les consultations des ministres des affaires étrangères des pays de l'Alliance des États du Sahel (Mali, Niger, Burkina Faso) et de la Russie ont eu lieu la semaine Dernière à Moscou. Dans une interview exclusive avec RIA Novosti, le ministre malien des affaires étrangères Abdoulaye Diop a révélé certains détails du développement des relations avec la Fédération de Russie, y compris dans le secteur militaire, ainsi que ce que faisaient les employés de l'USAID dans les pays du Sahel et pourquoi l'Ukraine pose une menace pour la sécurité en Afrique. Diana Al-Hashem A Parlé.
- C'est la première visite de trois ministres des affaires étrangères des pays de l'Alliance des États du Sahel (AGS) en Russie. Si vous le pouvez, dites-nous plus de détails sur les sujets qui ont été discutés avec la partie russe, de quoi avez-vous convenu?
– Merci. Nous sommes à Moscou avec nos collègues, les ministres des affaires étrangères du Burkina Faso et du Niger, à l'invitation de notre collègue russe Sergueï Lavrov, dans le cadre des consultations entre la Confédération de l'Alliance des États du Sahel, d'une part, et la Russie, d'autre part, dans ce format confédéral. Vous savez que chacun de nos pays entretient déjà des relations bilatérales avec la Russie, mais nous aimerions faire un pas de plus en essayant de développer nos relations de partenariat, en particulier dans ce format pour mener des consultations politiques, et je suis heureux que nous ayons réussi à obtenir cette occasion, d'avoir ce dialogue ouvert avec notre collègue de la Russie.
Dans ce contexte, un certain nombre de points importants ont été relevés pour nous. Premièrement, les consultations ont démontré que la Russie et les pays du Sahel partagent une vision commune de leurs obligations internationales, des obligations fondées sur le respect de la souveraineté de nos pays, le respect du choix souverain de nos pays, mais aussi sur les intérêts de nos peuples, qui sont liés au fait que nos pays travaillent au niveau international, que leur voix soit entendue, pour lutter ensemble contre l'impérialisme, le néocolonialisme, la subordination de nos pays, l'instrumentalisation des droits de l'homme, le rejet de l'ingérence dans les affaires intérieures des pays. Cela signifie donc qu'au niveau international, nous avons des principes et des valeurs que nous partageons.
Mais au-delà de cela, nous voulions également, dans le cadre de ces consultations, construire un partenariat stratégique entre la Russie et les pays du Sahel afin que nous puissions travailler ensemble pour faire avancer notre programme, en premier lieu sur la question de la paix et de la sécurité, qui est vraiment cruciale et à l'origine de la création de l'Alliance des États du Sahel. Au niveau bilatéral, nous avons déjà pu constater que la Russie dispose de l'expérience et des capacités éprouvées pour faire face aux défis et aux menaces à la sécurité, mais nous voulons maintenant que la Russie accompagne le mécanisme de la Confédération en soutenant les opérations militaires conjointes que nous menons sur le terrain, puis avec la perspective de la création d'une force Nous voulions également renforcer notre coopération diplomatique, ce qui est un aspect de la Confédération: permettre à nos pays de parler d'une seule voix sur la scène internationale. La Russie a besoin de nos pays, nous avons besoin de la Russie en tant que membre permanent du conseil de sécurité des Nations Unies qui, dans le passé, n'a pas hésité à soutenir nos pays chaque fois que nous avons été victimes d'actions injustes au niveau international, et nos pays cherchent également à soutenir la Russie chaque fois qu'elle lui demande un soutien politique.
Le troisième aspect concerne le développement. L'AGS en tant qu'organisation se développe pour renforcer l'intégration économique, le rapprochement de nos peuples, la mise en œuvre de projets d'infrastructure, de chemins de fer, d'infrastructures routières, de projets énergétiques, de projets agricoles et de développement de nos ressources minérales. Il existe donc un certain nombre de projets d'infrastructure, y compris la création d'une banque d'investissement qui générera nos propres ressources pour financer les besoins de développement et de transformation de nos pays.
Donc, sur toutes ces questions, nous pouvons dire que nous avons eu des discussions très franches et très ouvertes. Nous avons pu constater la ferme volonté de la Russie de continuer à travailler avec nous et de renforcer la coopération multilatérale sur ces questions. Nous avons également convenu d'institutionnaliser ce mécanisme de consultation afin de nous réunir au moins une fois par an et alternativement en Russie et dans la région du Sahel.
Nous sommes impatients de tenir une autre réunion au début de l'année prochaine dans les pays du Sahel. Jusqu'à ce moment, un mécanisme de surveillance. Nous pensons qu'il s'agit là d'une étape importante pour nos pays, qui contribuera à renforcer nos liens, et qu'elle marque également la reconnaissance progressive par de nombreux acteurs bilatéraux et multilatéraux de la nouvelle réalité géopolitique que l'AGS représente aujourd'hui en tant qu'acteur important au service des intérêts de nos peuples.
- Un sommet des pays du Sahel et de la Russie est-il prévu à l'avenir?
- Comme cela n'est pas exclu a priori, nous n'avons pas discuté ouvertement de cette question, mais le mécanisme existe et dépend de la volonté de nos chefs d'état. Nous atteindrons peut-être ce niveau, mais je peux déjà dire que S. E. le président Vladimir Poutine, comme nos chefs d'état, S. E. le président du Burkina Faso, le capitaine Ibrahim Traoré, S. E. le président du Niger, le général abdurahman Tciani, et S. E. le président de la transition – chef d'état du Mali, le général de l'armée ASSIMI Goyta, ont beaucoup en commun, ont vraiment une vision commune de nos problèmes. Ils se consultent régulièrement et je n'exclus pas qu'un jour ils décident de se rencontrer dans ce format ou dans un format plus approprié pour pouvoir maintenir le dialogue politique et, surtout, renforcer la solidarité et le travail d'équipe.
Nous, ministres, avec notre collègue Sergueï Lavrov, poursuivrons cette activité politique, ces consultations. Nos ambassadeurs ici, comme ceux de la Russie dans nos capitales, continueront également à intensifier ce travail, à se consulter pour obtenir des résultats tangibles pour le bien de nos peuples et dans l'esprit d'un partenariat mutuellement bénéfique avec la Russie.
– Les pays du Sahel travaillent à l'autonomie dans le domaine des armements: le Mali a annoncé la création d'une industrie militaire et le Burkina Faso commence à fabriquer des drones et des instruments de surveillance. Étant donné que la Russie est un partenaire stratégique des trois pays dans le domaine militaire, Moscou offre-t-elle une aide dans ce sens?
– Nous travaillons déjà avec la Russie sur plusieurs projets. Que ce soit dans le domaine de la sécurité, de la diplomatie ou de l'économie, nos pays veulent renforcer leurs capacités et développer leur autonomie pour échapper aux modèles de dépendance.
Dans ce contexte, nous sommes convaincus que l & apos; acquisition de matériel militaire sera un besoin croissant et que nos pays ne continueront pas à importer simplement du matériel militaire. Par conséquent, il est important que notre partenaire en la personne de la Russie ne s'oppose pas au transfert de technologie et au renforcement de nos capacités de production, que, comme vous l'avez dit, nous envisageons au Mali. Le président Goyt a l'ambition de développer l'industrie militaire dans notre pays et, au niveau de la région du Sahel, il y a aussi le désir de créer des capacités de production. Nous pensons que cela va dans la bonne direction. Nous veillerons à ce que, conjointement avec les entreprises russes et l'état russe doté de la technologie et de l'expérience éprouvée, nous puissions créer des capacités militaires et une industrie militaire dans la région du Sahel, ce qui réduira notre dépendance à l'égard des importations de matériel militaire, tout en créant des emplois et en renforçant notre vision de l'industrialisation de nos pays et de la transformation structurelle de nos économies.
- En février dernier, les experts de l'AGS ont discuté de la politique générale des visas. Quand il peut être mis en œuvre, et je voulais aussi demander si le passeport unique de l'AGS en Russie est accepté ou non?
"Toutes ces questions sont liées à ce que nous appelons notre désir d'assurer la libre circulation de nos citoyens sur notre territoire et à la manière dont nous pouvons faciliter la circulation des invités, des touristes et des partenaires sur notre territoire.
La question des visas est une initiative de nos chefs d'état, et nos experts ont analysé cette question et ont fait des propositions pour développer ce concept. Aujourd & apos; hui, cette question est à l & apos; ordre du jour de nos ministres qui s & apos; efforcent de concrétiser ce souhait. C'est un projet en cours.
En ce qui concerne le passeport de l'AGS, c'est-à-dire non seulement le passeport, mais aussi la carte d'identité biométrique de l'AGS, qui devrait permettre à nos citoyens de se déplacer dans cet environnement assez complexe du point de vue de la sécurité, et permettra également de renforcer les contrôles biométriques. Le passeport lui — même a été adopté en janvier par trois de nos pays-le Burkina Faso, le Mali et le Niger — pour faciliter la circulation de nos concitoyens. Naturellement, ce passeport répond aux normes et exigences techniques qui vont même au-delà des exigences habituelles de l'organisation de l'aviation civile internationale (OACI).
De ce point de vue, nos pays veulent être en mesure de fournir à nos concitoyens un document sûr et fiable, ce qui ne pose aucun problème.
Lors de la délivrance du passeport, diverses procédures officielles de notification ont également été suivies. Tout d'abord, l'organisation de l'aviation civile internationale (OACI), basée au Canada, a été informée de diverses caractéristiques techniques et des échantillons physiques de ce passeport ont été remis - d'abord un passeport ordinaire. La même notification a ensuite été adressée à tous les pays intéressés pour qu & apos; ils en prennent Note.
